    “I suppose I’m here to thank you,” Lena says, a sinister smile on her face. “The Underworld is absolutely thriving now after your little intervention.”

    “Surely I don’t know--” Lex starts, but Lena simply ignores him.

    “Trying to turn the dead against me with secrets and lies? That’s low, even for you.”

    “Now I know you didn’t come all the way here to flatter me,” Lex chuckles, shaking his head. “Lena, be reasonable. What would I want with a bunch of fluttering, useless, dead spirits?”

    He flashes a gleaming smile and Lena rolls her eyes.

    “It didn’t work,” Lena says flatly, her eyes burning with hatred. “Your little plan failed.”

    “Ah, no matter, you’re here now, aren’t you? So I guess you could say it was worth it. Sometimes I have to go through drastic measures just to get you to talk to me. Honestly, Lena, do we always have to be so dramatic?” Lex snaps his fingers and the lights come back on, sharper and brighter than before. Lena scowls at the obvious exaggeration and squints her eyes.

    “What do you want, Lex?”

    “You know exactly what I want, and I’ve been very clear about that from the start.” Lex’s eyebrow shoots up in contention and Lena feels some of the anger burn like liquor in her throat.

    “You never cared about her before, not in all the years --”

    Lex cuts her off with his overly bright smile.

    “Oh, I have always cared. Please, you make me sound like such a monster,” Lex chuckles brightly. “Isn’t that your role?”

    Lena’s jaw snaps shut as she scowls at her brother. She hates the way he practically preans during every conversation, like everything he says is a boastful declaration, even when it’s convoluted.

    “You made a huge mess of things when you turned your back on me, and yet I’ve left you alone. I’ve let you come and go as you please, and do that little thing with your ridiculous hospital, though for all the gods in the universe, I can’t understand the point of it. I don’t bother you for hardly anything. I don’t stumble into your house unannounced--”

    “--Because you’re too afraid of what might happen if you do--”

    Lex exhales in amusement before rolling his eyes.

    “Most souls prefer the sun, even you can understand that,” Lex says, pursing his lips as he regards her in disgust. “Sure, we’ve had our differences, little sister, especially when it came to the whole Krypton debacle, but I really thought we were past this. And all I’m asking for is the one thing you owe me.”

    “Why now?”

    Lex unclasps his hands and sits up straighter, his face drawn in serious thought. He looks at her with swirling eyes, and even though he looks crazed and on the verge of frenzy, Lena swears she can feel the palpable thump of fear radiating from his bones.

    “Kara is too dangerous. She has decided to show herself to the mortals and to the other gods. Now everyone knows for a fact that there is one Titan left. She is the one thing standing in my way, the one thing challenging my absolute rule. If it weren’t for you, she would have been handled properly long ago.” Lex leans forward, still staring at Lena with calculating eyes. It’s the look he gets when he thinks he’s putting one over on someone, and Lena clenches her fists in her robes. “I’m not angry anymore, Lena. I even offered her what I consider to be a very fair deal, which is more than she deserves. Yet once again, you’ve meddled in things that you have no business meddling in.”

    Lena clenches her jaw. She knows Lex would not have offered Kara a fair deal in any capacity. Sending her to Olympus would be a fate worse than death, where she would be forced into enslavement or something equally as appalling. There is no justice when it comes to her brother, only statements of power. She knows she’s backed into a corner now that he has his mind so focused on getting back what he feels he is owed, but Lena holds her ground.

    “So this is what your revenge looks like? You’ve taken some poor mortal to use for your bidding?” Lena retorts, narrowing her eyes in anger. She tilts her head and stares harshly, hardly noticing that the lights have dimmed to a more suitable glow. “Reign is a pathetic attempt at getting even and you know it.”

    Lex laughs so heartily that it startles her.

    “Oh, Lena, your sense of humor has always been my favorite thing about you! It’s almost like it gets better with the darkness!” Lex wipes tears from his eyes. As suddenly as his good humor appears, it vanishes, and he turns cold and hostile. “Did you really think you were the only one who took a Titan pet home with them?”

    “Kara is the last Kryptonian,” Lena declares, crossing her arms across her chest. “So I don’t know what you’re talking about.”

    “That’s where you’re wrong, my dear sister. I always knew you’d turn on me, so I had to be prepared,” Lex explains, his lips twisting into a sardonic smile. “And oh, you have no idea how long I have been waiting for this day.”

    “You’re a bottom feeder.”

    “Reign is from Krypton, same as Kara, but she’s got some...enhancements, if you will.” Lex’s fingers twist along his chin as he looks to the sky. He reeks of smugness and Lena knows he thinks he’s in full control. She bites the inside of her cheek and waits. Her heart pounds heavily in her chest, and she hates that Lex can hear it. “Now, I admit, Kara is a marvelous weapon -- so strong , with so much potential! But she’s wild, and untamed. This one is better. So compliant, and so easily controlled. And she will destroy Kara, make no mistake about that.”

    “That’s not--possible--” Lena breathes, trying to cover her own shock. Kara, to Lena’s knowledge, has always been the last surviving Titan, and the fact that she might not be makes her dizzy with fear.

    “I assure you, it is. You were always so distracted with your books, so foolishly trying to be like those Kryptonian Titans to pay attention to anything else going on. But I did. I watched Zor-El and the rest of them -- always studying and calculating. Always scheming like they could really outsmart me. They were all so weak, and so fearful, that they were too stupid to see they were using up all their resources. They did the work for us and destroyed themselves. On top of that, they left us all we needed for a biological weapon to secure our standing on top of Olympus. I never had to use her before. Now, I fear I must.”

    Something shifts in Lena’s stomach as Lex’s explanation punches into her with brute force. She swallows heavily, trying to connect the dots at a feverish pace. She thinks back to long ago, to the memories of a time she has tried so hard to block out. It comes in perfect sequence, like the pages in her books, highlighted with passages that scream for her attention.

    Lex interrupts her thoughts, and she forces her expression to remain neutral as she glances back at him.

    “Now, as I was saying. You can give Kara back to me, and this will all go away, or you can keep her, and watch the Earth burn. Do you really want to be responsible for the downfall of another race?”

    “Your lies will catch up with you,” Lena snaps, and Lex’s nostrils flare with indignation.

    “Oh, they won’t, but you’re sweet for caring. No, see, my words are absolute truth where it concerns you. This isn’t a far stretch, Lena,” he says, as he stands off the couch and begins to walk toward her. He waves his arms in grand gestures as he speaks, circling her like cornered prey. “The humans already think you poison children, and it was far too easy to spin that narrative. I thought you’d see that and come begging for mercy sooner. I can make them think anything I wish. I promise you, the mortals won’t know Reign as a worldkiller. They’ll only know you.”

    “You’re still threatening me, after all these years? That's rich.” Lena crosses her arms and forces herself to smile despite the persistent anger clawing in her chest.

    “I know you haven’t forgotten Krypton. This will be the same. The Titans all thought you were the reason for their demise. Tell me, have you told your precious Kara the truth about what you are?” Lex grins, so pleased with himself. Lena chokes back the urge to blast him across the sky. He reaches out and tucks a strand of her hair behind her ear, but before he can, she knocks his fingers away from her face. He smiles. “You’re pathetic for thinking Kara is any different from the rest of them. She has you right where she wants you, and any minute she can destroy you.”

    “You’re wrong,” Lena bursts, the tears welling behind her eyes, angry and hot and violent. “Kara knows everything, and she still chose to stay. You don’t know anything about her.”

    “I know that the dead have sworn their loyalty to her, have they not? They call her their Queen,” Lex says with a shrug. He smiles wickedly as he looks down on Lena from his slightly taller vantage point. She can smell the staleness of his wine-laden breath. “She holds the Underworld and the Earth in the palm of her hand, and you’ve made it so easy with your weakness for a pretty face. She’s playing the long game, and if you had any brains at all, you’d help me finish her for good. Restore the balance of the gods! Help your family keep what’s theirs!”

    “What we stole, you mean?” Lena feels herself coming unhinged, the anger bubbling and brewing violently beneath the surface. “You know what, Lex? I’d rather be destroyed by Kara’s hand than help you hurt her.”

    “She almost killed you once, or have you forgotten?” Lex shakes his head in disapproval. She imagines melting the knowing smirk off his face, and it gives her a brief release.

    “If I recall, like most unnecessary evil, that was heavily influenced by you,” Lena retorts, her lips curling into a challenging snarl. The horrifying memories of Kara fighting off the black kryptonite flash before her eyes and she bites her lip to keep herself centered.

    “Allegedly! Come on now. I wish I could take all the credit for that, but I can’t give away all my secrets.”

    “It doesn’t matter, because like most of your plans, it failed spectacularly,” Lena grins, the pride welling in her chest at Kara’s remarkable strength. “As I said, you don’t know Kara. You just have some pathetic puppet that you think you can control.”

    “Something like that,” Lex says, shrugging. Lena frowns at the way he seems unaffected by her rebuttals.

    “Show her to me," Lena demands.

    “Excuse me?”

    “Show me Reign," Lena says again, louder this time. “Bring her here. I want to see what all this hype is about.”

    “That’s not how it works, Lena. I don’t answer to anyone,” Lex snaps, his smug smile finally starting to falter. He glares at her in silence and Lena smiles at the shift.

    “Are you worried I'll see right through her? See that she's nothing more than smoke and mirrors?”

    “Think what you want," Lex responds. A clap of thunder echoes loudly outside, and Lena turns in the direction of the sound. He's hiding something, and her heart flutters at the thought. "I certainly don't take commands from someone beneath me."

    “This is insane!” Lena bursts, shaking her head in adamant opposition. "I'm not letting Kara come up here just so you can keep her as a trophy."

    “I thought you might say that,” Lex says, unconcerned. He turns on his heel and walks back toward the table, pouring himself another goblet of wine. He gestures to Lena, but she simply frowns at his offering. “Which is why she will come of her own accord. She has the same weakness of the heart as you do when it comes to these humans. She knows that they will all suffer if she isn’t returned to me, so there won’t be any question what her choice will be.”

    Lena scowls in silence as she considers the words.

    “I will get what I want, Lena,” Lex speaks directly, his voice booming like thunder. “I always do. And the harder you make it, the worse it’s going to be for Kara. What’s a little mortal blood when it comes to securing my kingdom?”

    Lena doesn’t answer right away. She watches as Lex shakes his head, clicking his tongue with pity as he watches her, like she’s some pathetic source of entertainment brought in to be mocked. Lena closes her eyes, and all she can see is Kara’s face. The crystal clearness of her eyes is so striking, Lena sucks in a breath. She doesn’t doubt that Kara loves her. There is no truth to Lex’s venomous words about Kara’s ulterior motives, and Lena knows it. Maybe she would have fallen for that earlier, but her heart is too wrapped up in Kara to consider anything but the pureness of her heart. And even if she were to be destroyed, just having these few months with Kara would make her entire existence worth it.

    She knows there are parts of Lex’s words that ring true, however. She has no doubt what Kara’s decision will be. She might love Lena, but she won’t be selfish. She will protect the mortals from peril because that’s who she is. And if the tables were turned, and Lena needed saving, Kara would do the next best thing. She would offer herself.

    It’s why Lena loves her more than anything in the universe. It’s why Lena will do anything to save her. It’s why she says the next thing that comes out of her mouth.

    “Take me instead.”

    The words shatter the silence, and Lena swears she can hear them echo off the walls as Lex’s eyes widen.

    “I’m sorry?”

    “You heard me perfectly fine,” Lena responds, her tone rigid and cold. “I’m offering you myself in her place.”

    “You’re a fool, Lena. An absolute fool!” Lex laughs heartily, but Lena simply watches. Lex’s amusement fades into a nervous chuckle until he’s scowling back at her. “You’re no one’s hero. What would I possibly want with you?”

    “The unlimited power over the dead, combined with your own? You’d be unstoppable. No one - not even a Titan - would be able to beat you.”

    Lex pauses, looking her up and down like he’s trying to sniff out a trick. Lena’s eyebrow raises precisely as she thinks thoroughly about her decision. It’s a dangerous, reckless chance she’s taking, but it’s all she’s got.

    “You’re serious?”

    “Deadly,” Lena hears herself say. Her mind is still busy calculating. “But you have to take the oath.”

    “The conditions?” Lex asks, taking a casual sip from his wine.

    “You stand down. Spare the mortals of Earth. And, absolutely no harm comes to Kara,” Lena says quickly. “Ever.”

    “I could ruin you,” Lex replies, the sharp lines in his forehead becoming more pronounced as he deepens his frown. He places his wine glass back on the table and points to her. “You realize this, right?”

    They stare each other down for several more minutes, Lex's lava-laced eyes erupting in volatile fits while he snarls in Lena's direction. She feels the silent negotiation as the energy buzzes between them, before Lex tilts his head slightly and eases back on his intensity.

    “Do we have a deal?” Lena finally asks, holding out her hand. Lex stares at it with skepticism, before reaching out and shaking.

    “Done.”

    Lena feels her knees wobble as their hands join together, and each pulse of their handshake makes her more queasy than the last.

    ”I’m holding a gala in a week. That will give you enough time to get things in order,” Lex says, releasing his grip on her hand and puffing out his chest. He picks his wine glass back up again. “I expect you both to be in attendance, ready and willing to comply. If you do, I’ll send Reign away for good and then...you belong to me.” He grins, hiding behind a nasty smile that has no love behind it and points in Lena’s direction. “If you refuse, you know what will happen.”

    Lena nods and swiftly turns on her heel. The walls feel like they’re closing in on her, choking all the life from her lungs as she desperately tries to put some distance between her and this place.

    “Oh and Lena?” Lex calls out, the pitch of his voice bordering on sing-song, like he’s got one more joke to tell that will have Lena seeing fire. She grimaces as she turns around.

    “Tell Kara to wear something festive,” Lex winks with a cheshire-cat smile. “I think I can find a pair of earrings to match that necklace.”

    Lena’s vision tunnels as she tilts her head and focuses on the center of his face, unleashing the frustrated scream that has been aching to leave her chest since she got to Mount Olympus. The lights flicker and all the bulbs explode with the shock, as the table next to Lex gets flipped and tossed completely across the room. The wine bottles shatter, sending the dark red contents spilling across the white floor like blood spurting from a wound. Lex’s glass shatters in his hand, splashing wine across his face.

    “You’ve got a little--” Lena points to her face, mimicking wiping off the spill as she stares at him with a sneer. “It’s a shame to waste such a delicacy.”

    Instead of crying out, Lex just starts to laugh like a madman, howling like it’s the funniest thing he’s ever seen. Lena feels the anger churn in her gut as his boisterous guffawing grates against her ears.

    “I hope you enjoyed that,” Lex says loudly as he comes down from his laughing fit, wiping the wine from his face. His eyes flash with sinister darkness as he looks at Lena again. “You’re going to be considerably more fragile after today.”

    Lena heads down the mountain trying desperately to outrun Lex’s hysterical laughter. Lightning flashes in the distance as thunder rolls in from the east, and Lena feels herself spiraling quicker than she could have anticipated. She has to get to the Underworld fast and save the rest of her energy, because she doesn’t have much longer until she’s completely powerless.

    But Kara will be safe. And that’s all that matters.

    The shift in the dreary stillness hanging over the palace is practically undetectable, except to the two inhabitants waiting eagerly for their missing piece. Kara feels the second Lena returns to the Underworld, and Krypto’s heads snap to full attention. A low growl emits from his throats, and Kara’s heart stumbles over itself like it’s mimicking Lena’s steps. Kara stands and heads to the door, pausing to listen for the sound that will promise safety. Instead, the energy in the kingdom feels different than the other times Lena has arrived. A strange, pulsing tension vibrates around the air, and Kara turns to Krypto whose fur is standing unapologetically at attention. Everything feels unsettled. Lena’s quiet, graceful footfalls and tempered breathing, sounds that Kara knows better than her own heartbeat, give way to something wild and unhinged. She listens to the way Lena’s breaths come shallow and uneven, and feels the way her heart beats erratically out of sync. Kara hurries down the hallway and races to the entrance of the palace with Krypto at her heels, both coming to a dead stop as Lena glides forward, looking ragged and enraged.

    “Lena!”

    Her eyes shift under her hood, and Kara takes note of how they flicker ominously with an amber glow like the final heat of iron before the branding. Gone are the whirlpools of endless gold, replaced by a stuttering light that struggles to remain constant. The parts of her skin that peek from the long sleeves of her cloak are sallow and dull, a stark contrast to the radiant ivory that normally illuminates the darkness. Kara swallows heavily as she watches Lena walk straight into the palace and head for her throne, a place she hardly ever enters anymore.

    Cat must have been following her, because the next thing she knows, Kara is exchanging a quick, worried glance to her fiery counterpart. It’s far from encouraging the way Cat seems to be as nervous as Kara feels.

    Lena takes a seat on her throne, her hair flowing in darkly unkempt and wild tendrils from under the hood of her cloak, chaotic and messy like the mane of an angry lion. She stares down harshly at the ground, and Kara can see the way the muscles of her jaw work furiously under the translucent skin of her face.

    When she speaks, her voice is hoarse, like she’s been screaming, and Kara’s heart plummets.

    “If my brother wants a war, then it’s a war he’s going to get,” Lena declares sharply, her voice a low rumble that makes Krypto respond with an equally menacing growl. She stares at Cat and Kara with one last jolt of fire in her eyes. They quickly fade to black, and Kara shivers. It feels like what little warmth they have in the Underworld has gone out completely, thrusting them all in icy night.

    “Well good, it’s about time,” Cat replies, eyeing her skeptically. Kara is thankful for her unwavering tone, so inappropriately perfect for the moment. “But I think you should get some sleep, first. You look dreadful.”

    “Thanks, Cat,” Lena rasps, her lips thinning into a muted smile. “Always encouraging.”

    “I mean it in the nicest way possible, but the Earth did not do you any favors.”

    Lena doesn’t respond and Kara watches as she slumps to the side slightly, propping herself tiredly against her arm. Kara closes the gap between them and reaches out to touch Lena’s hand.

    “Lena…”  

    “You aren’t mad?” Lena asks softly, her eyes slowly rolling skyward before landing on Kara. Her lips form a tired pout, and Kara strokes the back of her hand with her fingers. Lena’s eyes flutter closed.

    There she is. Hers. The sweet, gentle goddess that lights Kara’s heart on fire. Kara exhales in profound relief.

    “No, I’m not mad,” Kara says after a beat. “You’re going to kill me one of these days, but I’m not mad.”

    “I had to--”

    “I know.”

    There’s an awkward silence as Kara continues to study Lena’s haggard appearance. She’s still the most beautiful being Kara has ever laid eyes on, but there are startling differences that Kara can’t comprehend. Her eyes are sunken and dark, and her lips are quivering when she speaks. Kara feels the way her breaths come uneven and heavy, like she’s struggling for air.

    “Well then,” Cat clears her throat, as she heads for the exit. “I think we’ll have a lot to discuss, but for now, you need your rest. I’ll see you both tomorrow.”

    “Good night, Cat,” Kara mumbles, keeping her focus on Lena. If she looks away for even a second, the goddess of death might disappear.

    “Did it…” Kara starts, her fingers fumbling around Lena’s hand as she strokes her fingers gently. She isn’t sure what to say without blurting too much, too soon, but all she wants to know is what happened with Zeus. “Did it not go well?”

    Lena sighs. She gives a small smile before shaking her head sadly.

    “It was fine. He’s insufferable as always, but I think I bought us some time,” Lena shrugs, brushing it aside as she shifts in her throne. Kara pulls slightly on her hand, and Lena allows herself to be guided back to standing. “Can we talk about it tomorrow? I’m just so tired for some reason.”

    “Of course,” Kara says, holding a surprising amount of Lena’s weight against her hand as she turns to guide them both back to the bed chamber. “I’m just glad you’re home.”

    “Me too.”

    It takes more effort than usual to get settled into bed, as Lena’s movements seem clunky and slow compared to her usual graceful habits. Kara watches as she collapses into bed, pulling the blankets around her weakly. She goes to speak, but something seems to get stuck in her throat and she dissolves into a coughing spell for several long moments. Kara pats her back cautiously, wondering if she’s ever seen Lena look so frail.

    “Are you sure you’re okay? You’re trembling...” Kara asks again, feeling the way Lena practically vibrates under her touch. Her lips are frosted with a tint of blue, and Kara can almost see the puffs of breath as Lena exhales heavily in the dark.

    “Yeah, I’ll be alright,” Lena finally whispers, pulling the sheets around her tightly. “Just a long day.”

    “Here, come here.” Kara moves closer, wrapping her arms around Lena’s body and pulling her close. She almost gasps at the sensation of Lena’s frigid skin against her own.“You’re freezing.”

    “That’s because you’re always so warm, darling,” Lena says softly, sighing into the sheets as her body melts further into Kara’s. Her teeth are chattering loudly and Kara pulls her as close as possible, determined to pour all the heat she can into her body. She can barely hear Lena whisper into the darkness. “I love you, Kara.”

    Beyond the palace gates and down past the winding crags of slippery rock, miles from the village of the dead and out past the nearly endless river Styx, there’s a narrow path that exists only to the most unfortunate. The crumbling rocks slip under foot, shifting and sliding, becoming more unstable further down the treacherous trail. With only enough room to put one foot in front of the other, the rest of the landscape falls away leaving a sliver of ground high above scalding molten lava, precariously connecting the two parts of Hades’ realm: the mainland and the depths.

    The Underworld itself is a destination few deign to visit, but beyond the realm of Hades’ light, there’s a place that only exists in smoke and whispers. Tartarus, the home of the damned, is the prison where souls are placed after judgement, condemned to suffer infinite torment. As such, it’s the most terrifying place in all the cosmos, a reminder of the consequences for wickedness. It’s a place that few have seen with their own eyes, and still fewer have come back to speak the truth of its wretchedness. The demons of hell are said to cut out the tongues of trespassers, leaving them frantically mute in their attempts to convey the ghastly sights of the lower circle.

    The howls and screams echo off the walls as she walks further down the winding, twisting cavern into the scorned depths of the Underworld. She pulls her cloak tighter around her shoulders as she stumbles forward, aiming straight for the endless black hole of hell.  There’s a scratching sound that gets repetitively louder as the creatures of the dark hiss and writhe, clawing at her arms from behind their iron grates. She grimaces as they taunt her with their wicked tongues, the whispers loud and menacing as she forces herself to continue on the path.

    Hadesssss ...

    Lena tries to suppress the shiver that takes hold of her spine and rattles her bones as the demons call her name, their cold breath brushing over her vulnerable skin. Her eyes struggle to focus as she tries to squint into the dark, ignoring the impulse to turn on her heel and flee.

    Even surrounded by fire and brimstone, threatened by miles of bubbling lava, Lena’s skin prickles as her veins become icy with mortality. She rubs her arms in a sad attempt to ward off the chill, but all she feels are the small indents of wrinkles beginning to spiderweb along her skin. She bites her lip and trudges on, trying to forget the consequences of her actions on Earth and focusing on making one more reckless decision before the night is through.

    Her thoughts drift to golden hair splayed across a pillow, and warm, muscular arms that can bend steel and still wrap around her body with unmatched tenderness. This is why she’s here. Everything she’s doing must be to protect the angel of Krypton and the heart she’s placed in Lena’s hands.

    She arrives in front of a sealed off entryway, her palms sweaty with the dread of anticipation. She begins to wave her hands several times over the locks, frowning as the spell seems to fizzle and die from the tips of her fingers. The lock doesn’t budge, so Lena grabs it with her hands and meticulously picks her way through. Her hands quiver and shake as she tries to keep them steady, her wrists and forearms blazing in protest.

    The door finally opens, and Lena steps back as the orange glow of the fiery sky stabs the darkness within. She squints as she tries to sense the presence inside the jail, when she hears the unmistakable sound of shuffling feet.

    “Ah, Lena,” a craggy voice calls out, still hidden away in the darkness. Lena can feel the shadow skulking around and watching her with piercing, cruel eyes. No matter how hard she’s tried, or how many years have passed, she has never forgotten those hellish eyes. “While I admit it’s taken you longer than I expected, I’m glad you’re finally here.”

    Lena stiffens as everything goes deathly quiet. All she can hear is the hammering of her heart, and the slow, precise footsteps of the demon in the dark. The owner of the voice begins to emerge from the shadows, and Lena stares at the long flowing cloak that hangs like the decaying rags of the dead. It drapes off a tall skeleton-like body that stands towering over Lena by inches, causing her to lose her breath as she takes the sight in fully.

    “Now come,” the voice says, taking a final step forward and opening her arms with a sinister smile that curls over her sharp, shining teeth. “Give your mother a hug.”

    Several Months Earlier

    “This is the one,” a raspy voice whispers excitedly, pointing through the dense fog. The heavy haze within the crystal ball curls and swirls until it retreats to the edges, hanging briefly in quiet suspense. Slowly, the outline of a face materializes within the depths, starting with blurry features until each spin of smoke reveals another layer of detail. Deep brown eyes blink steadily ahead, laser focused, as the handsome figure of a woman walks confidently forward. She adjusts the lapels of her midnight black blazer. Her jaw is set, creating a sharp feminine line. The rest of her face is stoic, her entire demeanor brave.

    “She’s perfect.”

    As the owner of the voice continues to stare at the image in the ball, a shining string of twine appears in her hands. She begins to twist and weave the glowing thread between her fingers. Clothos, the spinner of fate, turns and grins at her sisters.

    “She’s human,” scoffs a second voice, nudging in for a closer look. She pops an eye into place, blinking as it bulges before settling into the empty socket. “They’re all the same.”

    “Not this one,” Clothos argues. “This one is different. I can feel it.”

    “So let’s get on with it already! It’s been a thousand years!” a third voice cries. “Vengeance!”

    “Patience!” The other two hiss. “This is why you’re not in charge, Atropos!”

    “I have more power than you two,” she argues, raising her scissors in the air. “One snip, that’s all it ever takes!”

    “Enough!” Clothos bellows. The other two sisters cower in silence. “This human’s fate has been sealed since her creation. She is chosen to merge with the Dark One. She is the only one strong enough.”

    The vision in the ball angles slightly as the woman’s chin lifts in defiance, daring the Fates to come closer.

    “She will die,” Atropos warns, stepping forward slightly. “They all do.”

    “Ah, yes, but when she does, everything will be different.”

    “How can you be sure it’s her?” Lachesis asks. “They all look the same.”

    “It has always been her, if you ever cared to pay attention.” Clothos rolls her eyes at her sisters. “The spell is clear as day: Reign cannot achieve full power until bound to the Earth by another. This is the vessel. Reign will commandeer her until there is nothing left, grind her to stone. She will rise, and the Earth will crumble.”

    “Pity,” Atropos sighs. “I rather like humans. They’re cute the way they think they have control.”

    “I say good riddance,” Lachesis complains. “And I don’t trust this one, either. Humans are too unpredictable. Her string changes even now, in your hands! This will never work!“ She reaches for the string tucked around Clothos’ fingers. “I say we do it my way.”

    Clothos pulls it out of her reach, scowling over her shoulder as her sister continues to paw at her.

    “We do not decide fate! We only dispense it. Do not forget your place, dear sister. That is most unwise.”

    “Well let’s get on with it! I’m not getting any younger!” Atropos calls out.

    “Or any better looking,” Lachesis mumbles. She retreats, crossing her arms. Her bony elbows poke through as the large sleeves of her cloak rise up slightly. “Fine, fine. I will watch as this all unravels. If nothing else, this will be wildly entertaining. You remember the last time...”

    She reaches forward and swipes the shared eye from Atropos, who snarls in displeasure.

    “We don’t need another episode--”

    “It’s time!” Clothos cries out, clapping her hands excitedly. The room falls silent. She pulls back her hood, revealing a skeletal face with missing eyes. She holds up the string. “Sisters! The fate of the Earth resides in our hands. Reign must awaken!”

    The Fates begin to chant as Lachesis takes the string, extending it outward in grand ceremony.

    Down below, the Earth shakes violently, rattling and shifting with the cosmic power that has been unleashed from above.

    A deep, primal voice bellows from beyond.

    “I have awoken.”

    Sam Arias bolts upright in bed, her blood surging wildly, pulsing in time with the quaking Earth. Her breaths come in short, hot gasps as she clutches her chest, feeling the drum of her heart pounding against her ribs. She’s soaked to the bone, sweating through her nightshirt as she trembles uncontrollably. Her muscles feel hot and fiery as she cranes her neck to find the source of the voice that disturbed her.

    The Earth settles, but the silence is deafening.

    She’s all alone in her room, but there’s a presence somewhere in the depths of her soul that she can’t seem to shake.

    Present Day

    Lillian’s touch is somehow colder than Lena remembers; sharp, frigid fingers grip along her arms without a trace of life in their tips. The reception shouldn’t come as a surprise, so Lena tries to ground herself in what she knows. Her mother has never been the warm, loving type even in times of great prosperity. It would be laughable to trick herself into thinking that hundreds of years locked away in the depths of hell would soften her mother’s spirit. As soon as they make contact, Lena’s entire body explodes in reminiscent agony, her mother’s touch shrapnel ripping violently through her veins.

    Lillian is tall and angular, with limbs that twist and twirl in elegant lines. Her eyes are shifty, darting with cat-like precision as they focus intensely on every excruciating detail. They never miss a beat; she can detect even the slightest hair out of place, and Lena doubts the time in the depths has changed this fact. She feels the way her mother’s arms tentatively wrap around her in a stiff hug, one that’s lacking in love and heavy with years of pent up resentment. She’s conscious of the way her mother’s eyes move rapidly, assessing her appearance, and everything it lacks. She listens to the chains as they rattle -- a harsh reminder of their reality -- and Lena’s shoulders fall heavily as she shifts out of her mother’s grip.

    Lillian has been locked away for lifetimes, banished long before the fall of Krypton. In fact, the door to her infinite prison has never been opened until this very moment. Despite the circumstances, she stands tall and smug with a knowing smile stretched across her face, like she expected this reunion. By all accounts, Lena reasons, she probably did. The wretched arrogance of her family makes Lena’s skin crawl. Even with death in the palm of her hands and the keys to her mother’s freedom, Lillian still manages to make her feel inferior.

    Lena forcibly reminds herself that it’s necessary to keep her locked away like this. Lillian can’t be trusted, no matter how much Lena has always been willing to try. She knows better, but there’s a guilt that gnaws at her, even now. The feeling is more insufferable than ever. It’s for the good of the world that Lillian is out of reach -- both for the Earth and the planets beyond -- but it doesn’t come as easily to Lena as it should. Her mother’s lockdown is still another burden she’s had to shoulder, along with the infinite slander of her own name: just the endless consequence to being Hades. Lena squares her shoulders and stares up at her mother’s piercing eyes. There’s no love lost between them, yet something shifts between her ribs. There’s a persistent yearning for acceptance that aches deep in her heart, as strong and as ill-timed as always.

    Lena sighs, feeling the cold fatigue settle on her limbs. There’s no use dwelling on childish desires. Lillian is a cunning manipulator, and that will never change, no matter what Lena tries to do or say. She deserves her prison sentence, even if she’s the only mother Lena has ever known.

    She grinds back the tears and forces herself to remain impassive. Now is not the time to show weakness. It’s a skill she learned from many years under Lillian’s care, the irony a bitter pill to swallow.

    “You look well.” Lillian’s voice cuts through the darkness, her eyes shining with devious meaning.

    Lena feels the anger coil deep in her gut. She forces a smile. “You’ve always been great at lying.”

    Lillian’s sharp, orange-tinted eyes scour over Lena’s face, clawing to the center of her soul. Her lips curl over razor pointed teeth.

    “What am I supposed to say?” She hisses, wearing the disapproving frown she always seems to display around Lena. “Your exploits on Earth are far from commendable. Even for you, this is over the top.”

    “I didn’t come here to exchange pleasantries.”

    “No, I suppose not. You’re on a bit of a tight timeline these days, aren’t you?”

    Lena feels the blood drain from her face. She inhales sharply, the damp mist clogging her throat in protest as it kicks into her lungs. Her newly-mortal body trembles in desperation as she grits her teeth to force her expression to remain neutral. Anything to prevent giving Lillian the satisfaction of seeing her squirm. She knows it comes too late, as Lillian nods with a triumphant snarl.

    “Oh Lena, your foolish heart has gotten you in trouble again. When will you ever learn?”

    Lena exhales forcefully and turns on her heel. This has been a mistake. As desperate as she is for answers, she is not going to subject herself to the scorn and ridicule of a mother who probably won’t help her in the first place. Not without wanting something in return. There are other ways to solve her dilemma -- ones that don’t involve suffering unnecessary harassment.

    “No!” She hears Lillian cry out. Lena stops, her foot shaking, itching to continue forward. She contemplates taking another step, one that will close the door on her mother for good. It will never be different. Her brain urges her to think rationally -- to do the thing she has always been too weak to do. There’s heavy silence, and Lena can hear the steady heartbeat of the woman behind her. It thuds miserably, calling to her on a level only she can seem to feel. The pulse aches in her throat. Lena, it seems to drone. Help me.

    Inevitably, Lena’s heart wins out. She pauses, and it’s just long enough for her to resign herself. She knows she will hear what Lillian has to say. What’s more, she knows she may never have the strength to push her away entirely. She curses herself internally.

    “No, I promised myself if I ever got the chance to speak with you again, it would be different. I’m sorry.” Lillian’s voice sounds as close to sincere as it can be, and Lena forces herself to turn back around. She walks back to where her mother is standing, careful to keep her arms crossed tightly against her chest.

    “Yes, well, old habits die hard,” she says pointedly, wondering if the expression on her face is as sharp as she means for it to be. Lillian’s pursed lips give no indication either way, and Lena sighs.

    They stare in harsh silence at each other, Lillian in chains, but her eyes watchful and luminous in the darkness. Lena shifts uncomfortably under her gaze. She clears her throat and finally finds her voice.

    “I need you to tell me about Reign.”

    Lillian hesitates, and Lena swears she can see a flicker of fear on her face. A fear she was hoping for, but it startles her when it actually happens.

    “He wouldn’t show her to me,” Lena says, careful to keep her face stoic. She watches the way Lillian stiffens, her sharp eyes cutting across her like icy daggers. Still, she refuses to flinch. Lena presses on. “He won’t show me Reign because he can’t. She isn’t in his control. She’s in yours.”

    Lillian grins at this, staring off into the distance beyond Lena’s shoulder with a triumphant smile. When they lock eyes, Lena feels the smugness wafting off of her as she clicks her tongue condescendingly.

    “While I appreciate the sentiment, I hate to disappoint you. Reign is made by old Titan magic. The witches of Krypton created her long before the existence of Rao, or such is my understanding. It’s a magic I didn’t believe carried over into the new world, but I was mistaken.” Lillian pauses, the disgust apparent on her face at having missed a very crucial detail. “She takes over a mortal vessel, one that has has been left up to the power of chance, but she is not under any of our control. That’s what makes her particularly dangerous. She has no alliance, though your brother will have you and everyone else think otherwise.”

    “She’s acting independently of his orders?”

    Lillian rolls her eyes impatiently. “Yes.”

    Lena swallows, her throat closing around this information. “What does she want?”

    “She is meant to dispense justice, carried out by the old order. The ancient witches wanted to have a way to cleanse society and begin fresh, should the need ever arise. Once the Titans knew Krypton was dying, some of them managed to call upon this lost entity. They sent Reign to Earth in the hopes that she would rise, and eradicate the planet of lesser beings. It’s a feeble attempt to keep their pathetic race going. Reign is sent to Earth to begin a new Krypton.”

    “But Lex--”

    “Would rather spin the story in his favor. The King of the Gods doesn’t look so powerful if he allows something like this to be out of his control, Lena.”

    Her heart drops. “That’s why he wanted Kara.”

    “She’s the only one powerful enough to face her. Reign is, after all, of her blood.” Lillian snarls, and a chill rushes through Lena’s body. “But as fate should have it, Kara is instead here with you, hiding while the Earth burns.”

    Lena retreats momentarily into herself, trying to detangle what this all might mean. As much as she wants to fight the reputation forced upon her due to her brother’s meddling, the caustic slurs against Hades suddenly have more bearing than ever before. It truly is her fault -- Reign, the terror on Earth, Kara’s absence, everything. All because she fell for her brother’s trap and wanted to help him gain power once upon a time. Then she turned and tried to save and protect Kara, someone she was foolish and selfish enough to love.

    She knows better. She has always known better.

    She feels sick.

    Lillian watches her harshly, amusement dancing haughtily on her lips. Lena forces herself to focus.

    “Kara won’t help him,” she says, clenching her jaw tightly. “That is certain.”

    “She’ll help you, though. She’ll do anything for you, and you’ve certainly backed yourself into a corner,” Lillian counters. It’s a swift move, and one that Lena can’t argue with, no matter how hard she tries to deflect it. Lillian continues. “You’re going to have to let her go eventually. It’s the only way to defeat Reign. Keeping her here is only making everything worse, and you don’t want to be responsible for even more death, do you, dear?”

    Lena raises her chin in defiance. The stab of her mother’s words deflect off her with little force. A minor sting, her skin is numb after years of the same daggers being plunged into her soul. It’s pleasing that her mother’s ammunition has somehow gotten weaker over time, even if it only means Lena is too tired to care anymore.

    “It’s all a shame, really, the way our family has crumbled,” Lillian begins to edge further into the light, forcing Lena to take a step back. “Lex is brilliant, but too arrogant. A hot head, whose temper will always be his downfall. But you-- you are cold and equally as fiendish. Think of it! Your intellect, and your abilities, with a weapon like Reign on your side and a command of Death, you could be great.”

    “Other than my brother’s abnormal obsession with me and my life, I AM great,” Lena declares, holding her position. She stares into Lillian’s eyes.

    “That was then. What you are right now is tragically...ordinary. A mortal.” Lillian’s lips curl. Lena feels a chill run through her as she stands, exposed. “Why do you want to be like them? Why do you waste countless hours pandering to the useless humans of Earth? You cling to them so desperately, when you have all THIS.” Lillian gestures around. Lena follows her outstretched hand, but her eyes track along the ground.

    The depths of hell are no paradise, no matter how much power she may have once possessed.

    “And you could be so much more,” Lillian drawls on. She leans closer. “Why would you want to be anyone other than Hades?”

    “You’ve never taken an interest in me before, unless it was for your own gain,” Lena argues, crossing her arms to protect herself from the needling words Lillian weaves in her direction. “Why now?”

    “Because you’re more like me than you realize,” Lillian explains. “We need to stick together. If it’s answers you want, then I can help you achieve greatness. No one will get in your way.”

    “I don’t need your help. I’m perfectly capable on my own.”

    “Is that why you came to me? To show me how powerful you are?” Lillian’s eyebrow quirks knowingly. Lena bites her lip, noting the same habit. Sometimes, it’s like looking in a mirror, even for the briefest of seconds. She hates herself more with every glance at her mother. “I have always loved you, Lena, in my own way. Let me prove it to you, now.”

    “And how exactly do you plan to do that?”

    “Simple,” Lillian shrugs, grinning. She purses her lips as she studies the chains that bind her. When she meets Lena’s eyes, it’s as if she’s practically giddy with the thought. “I will help you get the revenge you’ve always wanted. Between the two of us, we can take your brother down. Then you’d be free to rule all the cosmos. And, after all, isn’t that what you’ve always really wanted?”

    Lena pauses to consider, though she hates that she does. She hates that there is still a fire deep in her gut, coming to life with the promise of revenge. She’s forgiven Lex long ago for all his transgressions - at least the ones against her - but the image of Kara’s beautiful face dredges up the slick, heavy feeling of hatred. She clenches her jaw to prevent herself from crying out and forces her gaze back to her mother. There is no way she can be trusted. Millenniums kept in solitude may have softened her, but she can’t expect her mother to have changed so much on her own. Can she?

    “That’s not--” Lena begins, her words already jumbled. “I don’t want to rule the universe.”

    “Don’t you?” Lillian crosses her arms in a challenge. “Isn’t that why you’ve held on to this grudge against your brother for so long? I know you’re upset that Lex outsmarted you and hurt your poor, little heart--”

    “--at least I have a heart--” Lena bites back, feeling the way it pounds painfully against her ribs. She’s never wished for its silence more, but it protests against her will, as strong as ever.

    “An overrated organ, romanticized by poets. Honestly, Lena. He played you like a game of cards and won the throne, and you’ve never been able to let it go, despite being left alone to do as you wish. You’ve had so many chances to work with your brother, to come back into the fold, and each time you’ve turned him down. Why else do you burn with rage?”

    Lena tries to swallow, feeling the way her throat is thick with ancient anger and the rage of all the lifetimes she’s struggled to contain. For the most part, she’s been successful at burying it -- turning her hatred into something purposeful and wholly good. Her desire for revenge and her disappointment in her family has forced her to be the exact opposite of them. But what does it say when after only a few moments in her mother’s presence, her baggage is apparently visible and hanging from her very limbs?

    Maybe I’m not as good as I thought I was, Lena considers. The thought squeezes down on her with unnecessary force, as her opinion of herself was already fairly low to begin with.

    “Why should I trust you?” Lena whispers into the darkness.

    “There is so much you don’t yet know,” Lillian says quietly. It’s an offering, though slight. Lena’s ears perk up. “But if you give me a chance, I will tell you everything. With everything I know, you won’t be able to lose.”

    The alarm bells go off in her head, clear and loud as ever. Lena ponders what it would mean -- to have a mother that actually cared. To have an ally in her own family, one that decides to actually choose her. But instead of feeling like the foolish young girl who craves attention and devotion, Lena’s thoughts turn sour at the fact that it’s too late for her. It’s too late for this. Even if Lillian has changed, and this is all part of some elaborate plan, the damage is so complete that Lena wonders if she can ever recover. What’s more, she’s furious at all the time she’s missed.

    Even with all the power in the world, there is no getting that back.

    “And what about Kara?”

    “Do you have to be so emotional? It’s disappointing.” The chains rattle as Lillian flexes against them angrily. She looks up toward the Earth in desperation. “You’ve moved the stars for that girl, when you could have been going after something far greater. Love has made you weak, Lena. More than that, it’s made you mortal. You’ve done enough for Kara. It’s time to focus on your family.”

    “My family,” Lena repeats, the words burning on her tongue. “Because they’ve done so much for me.”

    Lillian lunges forward dangerously, her face inches from Lena’s own. The chains rattle as they stretch, with Lillian straining against them. Lena doesn’t blink.

    “Your family is the only reason you are even here,” Lillian hisses through clenched teeth. “This could have all gone much differently if it weren’t for us. I would think you’d be a little more grateful, Lena. It could easily have been you in these chains.”

    Lena’s mind flashes to the screaming anguish of her mother at the moment Lena locked the chains -- when it was apparent that Lex was going to betray Lillian, and that he had Lena’s help to do it. Lillian’s eyes had torn deep into Lena’s soul with such a look of hurt, that it had haunted her dreams for millenniums.

    Back then, it was Zeus and Hades against the world. But their team up was  a short lived stepping stone on Zeus’ tyrannical rise to power. He used Lena to capture Lillian, to get her out of the way of the throne for good, under the guise that Lena was the only one powerful enough to do it.

    In retrospect, Lena was the only one foolish enough to fall right into his trap. She had lept head first at the promise of unconditional, familial love.

    It’s how Lex always got the better of her. He would get nostalgic and cryptic, and she would get emotional, and he’d have the upper hand.

    Pathetic.

    “Love is blinding at the start. It distracts. It makes you careless,” Lillian accuses, staring directly through her. “Power, true power, never fades. It’s not too late to make the right choice.”

    “And you speak of this love from experience?” Lena spits, indignant. The words ‘Lillian’ and ‘love’ have never gone together in any form of Lena’s reality.

    “Kara is wasting away down in the depths, playing house with you, and whether she resents you now or later, make no mistake: she will turn on you, and you will end up alone. You will have no one.” Lillian chuckles. The sound echoes off the walls, unwelcome in a place of such horror. “What will she think?” she asks finally, her eyes flashing bright and burning. “When she finds out you’ve made a deal with her enemy? Imagine, the scandal!”

    “I did it for her--”

    “And for yourself. You think you can outsmart him, and that’s why you’re here. Face it, Lena. You will be the enemy, just the way we always were to her kind. Legacies like that don’t go away quietly. Whether you like it or not, she needs to go back to Earth and take care of this problem that her ancestors have created. I don’t know how else to get that through to you.”

    The silence is cavernous, except for the distant dripping of water off the damp rocks above.

    “It was you.”

    Lena’s mind flashes back to Kara’s deadened eyes, the Black Kryptonite flowing through her veins. She unconsciously touches her throat, the place she can still feel Kara’s steel grip squeezing the life from her.

    “Oh darling, please. That was merely a… nudge, in the right direction.”

    “A nudge.” The scoff escapes Lena’s lips before she can stop it. “You almost had me destroyed.”

    “I think that’s a bit dramatic,” Lillian shrugs, unbothered by the entire affair. “But it certainly showed you what Kara is capable of, didn’t it?”

    Lena clenches her jaw to keep from spitting.

    Lillian smirks. “Besides, you’ve gone above and beyond to make sure to destroy yourself without any of my interference. You need my help. And I’m offering it to you for nothing.”

    “Oh I highly doubt that--”

    “The fact is,” Lillian cuts in, riding the wave of momentum. “Despite your best intentions, you stole what does not belong to you, and she must be returned. There is not much more to say about it. Unless--”

    “She came here by choice. And she can leave whenever she pleases,” Lena cuts in. “That has always been the way of it.”

    “Has it? Even when you bestowed magic upon her?” Lillian sneers, and Lena’s blood runs cold.

    The laws of the Underworld are complex, a labyrinth of loopholes and technicalities. It’s true, there may be some Lena doesn’t know. But she knows what Lillian is implying. She changes the subject quickly, back to her real reason for visiting.

    “Who is Reign?”

    “I believe you’ve already met her. Charming girl, perfectly average,” Lillian supplies, her eyes sparkling with amusement. “And, as fate would have it, much closer to you and your brother than you might imagine.”

    Lena stares at the ground. She already had an inkling, but to have it confirmed takes the wind from her lungs just a bit.

    “Necessary sacrifices, my dear. Nothing for you to get so torn up over,” Lillian says, shaking her head. “Think of the greater good.”

    “Because that’s what we’re all about, right? Our family is so good.”

    “If you bothered to see our side of it, I think you’d be surprised,” Lillian responds curtly. “I’m offering you a deal. I will help you get your revenge on your brother and make sure he never has absolute power over anyone ever again, if you accept my help.”

    “And what’s in it for you?”

    “My son, despite all the love I’ve given him, is the reason I’m down here,” Lillian explains, hanging her head. “It’s hard to keep a relationship when one is always wishing you dead.”

    “Not at all,” Lillian steps into the light fully, her chains pulled to capacity. She extends her hand out. “But it’s a chance we’re both going to have to take. Do we have a deal?”

    To put into words the concept of time in the Underworld is to accomplish the impossible, but it doesn’t stop mortals and immortals alike from trying. It could be anything and nothing, and all of it would be right.

    “This is all my fault,” Kara speaks again into the silence, her voice watery with regret. “I’m so sorry.”

    Lena doesn’t respond, but instead takes her time to sit upright. When she finally comes to, she looks at Kara with exhausted sadness.

    “It’s not the fields, Kara. I promise you. I will be just fine,” Lena stifles a yawn with the back of her hand before reaching out for Kara’s once more.

    “You don’t look fine.”

    “I know, darling. You’re sweet to me,” Lena sighs. “But I promise it will all be fine. Nothing stays the same, not even in the Underworld. Not even us.”

    Lena flinches slightly at this, and Kara exhales heavily, feeling the frustration leave as quickly as it came. She tries to carefully sit back down on the bed.

    “I’m sorry, but you must know what it is,” Kara insists, interlocking their fingers together. She studies Lena’s lips, and the way the color seems to have rushed from them in urgency. “I’ll...do more. I can help you more with whatever you need so you can rest. Anything.     Alex squints her eyes, scrutinizing the way the doorknob of the front door jiggles back and forth. She inches closer, clutching at the base of her gun, knuckles white and heart pounding in her ears. She’s sure whoever is on the other side can probably hear her ragged breaths as she tries to get her breathing under control. Sloppy , she berates herself. Focus, Danvers.

    She can’t afford to slip. Not right now.

    Her arms are tense and outstretched, the gun pointed at the entrance to the house. It’s early evening, and the sun has yet to go down, but that doesn’t mean danger isn’t lurking around every corner.

    The robber is bold, Alex credits, attempting to break into a house in what is practically broad daylight. She watches in silence, holding her breath and studying the way the latch slowly turns to unlock.

    “Walk away,” Alex whispers to herself, trying to impose her will on the stranger hidden from sight. “Just walk away…”

    “Hey, I’m home!” a voice announces cheerfully from behind the door. A foot crosses the threshold of the house and hurries inside. “Would you believe I couldn’t find my keys? I had to rummage around for the spare…”

    Sam places her keys and phone in the bowl by the door and turns to face forward. “I’m---Alex! What the hell?”

    A purse clunks to the ground as she stares, wide-eyed and panicked in Alex’s direction.

    “Sam!” Alex cries out, fumbling with her gun. She catches it just at the last minute and places the safety back on. “What are you-- how are you--”

    “Easy there officer!” Sam laughs, holding her hands up in surrender. “I promise I live here.” She bursts into her trademark goofy smile, and Alex’s heart fumbles in her chest. “Do you always answer the door like that?”

    “I’m--I--” Alex mumbles, too shocked to form a coherent sentence. She places the gun back in the holster on her side, which she’s wearing purely out of habit, and not because she’s going crazy with paranoia. “You’re...back?”

    Sam frowns as she slowly takes off her coat. “I told you I was going away for work,” she says carefully, turning away from Alex as she hangs it up. “Is everything okay? You look like you’ve seen an actual ghost.”

    “You didn’t tell me that,” Alex replies, following Sam as she walks down the hall into the kitchen. She isn’t too sure how far off Sam’s assessment is. Maybe this is a ghost. Maybe all of the stress is finally catching up to her. It wouldn’t be her first encounter with beings from the Underworld. “You’ve been gone for weeks, Sam.”

    “What do you mean?”

    “You left in the middle of the night -- no note, no explanation. You just-- disappeared. It’s been 3 weeks since I’ve heard from you.”

    Sam doesn’t reply. She stares at the kitchen island, before turning to grab a glass from the cabinet. Alex watches as she returns to the sink and fills it with water. Suddenly, she has an overwhelming urge for a drink herself. The stiff kind with a proof label that is preferably double her age.

    “Sam,” Alex prods gently, waiting as patiently as she can for some kind of acknowledgement. It still doesn’t come, as Sam’s throat tenses while she takes a sip of her drink. “I’ve been terrified for you. I filed a missing person’s report and everything. Where -- where did you go?”

    Sam starts to answer, but her response is cut off by the sound of breaking glass. Water cascades everywhere and shards of glass explode around her, but Sam doesn’t flinch. She just continues to stare through Alex, a single tear flowing down her cheek.

    “Sam?”

    “I don’t know,” Sam finally says, her voice breaking with the strain. She snaps back to herself and assesses the damage to the glass. She starts looking for the dish rag before Alex can reach out and stop her. Sam finally brings herself to look Alex in the eye, and there’s so much pain that Alex has to clench her jaw to keep from crying herself. “I don’t know. I-- I can’t remember anything from the past several weeks. I don’t know where I went.”

    “It’s still happening, then,” Alex replies softly. “The blackouts.”

    Sam nods, absently, and then finally looks back at Alex. Her face is desperate, quivering, before she bursts into tears.

    Alex pulls her close and holds her tight, but it doesn’t seem nearly enough. She partially expects Sam to just evaporate from her grip, to turn to dust right in front of her.

    “Alex, what am I going to do?” Sam wails, clutching at the collar of Alex’s shirt. She’s pleading, and searching, but there are no answers to be found between them.

    “Do you remember anything? Anything at all?”

    Sam shakes her head and sniffles, before pawing at the tears with the back of her hand. She pulls away from Alex and covers her mouth.

    ‘Another community is reeling in the aftermath of a planned attack. It seems to be the work of National City’s most wanted criminal, the masked terrorist known only as Reign--’

    Alex jolts at the voice, forgetting that she had left the TV on in all the commotion. She pauses to look at the screen. The image is frozen on the unmistakable figure of Reign, her face covered completely by a black mask. There’s something familiar about her, with the way she stands, poised and confident, her eyes dark and determined. Alex steps away from Sam and squints at the TV, trying to make sense of what she’s seeing.

    Reign’s limbs are long and lithe, and they’re positioned in such a way that Alex swears she’s seen it before -- but not only on TV.

    She glances back at Sam, who is staring at her with the same intensity held in those same deep, dark brown eyes.

    Alex glances back at the TV, then swallows the lump forming in her throat.

    “What’s happening to me?” Sam asks, following Alex’s gaze and looking at the TV.

    The silence is deafening. Alex gingerly walks back toward Sam, trying to figure out if she’s playing the long game, or if her girlfriend is truly a victim of the situation. It’s impossible to tell, as the tears flow steadily down her cheeks. She’s either a fabulous actress, or suffering beyond measure. Alex hates that she has to be the one to decide.

    Sam’s eyebrows furrow in confusion as she pleads silently for Alex to fix it.

    “Sam, I promise, this is only for your own good,” Alex explains, making a split second decision. She hates herself in the moment, but not more than Sam is about to. She reaches behind her and unhooks the handcuffs. “Only until we can figure out what’s wrong.”

    “What are you doing?” Sam’s eyes widen, before glaring back at Alex. Her face falls with betrayal, and Alex wishes for the Earth to swallow her whole. “You can’t lock me up!”

    “I’m sorry,” Alex says while choking back the tears that threaten to escape her lips. She swallows and forces herself to focus. It’s the only way to keep Sam -- and everyone else -- safe. The cuffs clink into place, as she gently pulls Sam’s arms behind her back. “You have the right to remain silent….”

    “Alex!” Sam cries out, protesting against Alex’s arms, her hands limp and uselessly locked together. “I didn’t do anything wrong!”

    “I know. We’re going to get you help, Sam. I promise. I just need you to trust me.”

    Kara’s dress is adorned in golden sunlight, the amber waves rippling with every step she takes. The fabric is sleek and airy, sparkling brightly against the dark canopy of night above them. It feels magical, like every fiber has been infused with the ancient powers of long ago. When Lena presented her with the dress, Kara couldn’t imagine wearing something so elegant. Her two worlds collide in the pattern of the garment-- the flowing wheat from the Elysian fields, mixed with the rays of the sun from above -- dancing together and infusing her with endless strength. Despite the circumstance of the affair she’s wearing it for, she’s proud to show it off. It makes her feel whole.

    It feels like her .

    Her hair is layered in blonde waves, cascading to her shoulders, with only a singular braid running through it. As she walks past a small pond, she almost doesn’t recognize the reflection staring back at her. The soft glow from the carefully hung lanterns catches her just right, causing a trail of flames to illuminate around her body.

    It’s otherworldly, and for the first time, she walks on Earth knowing exactly who she is. The knowledge of her bond to Lena, to the Underworld, and the magic coursing through her veins is no longer a curse, but a source of strength she didn’t know she needed. She glances over to the goddess next to her and offers a confident smile.

    “You’re with me, right?” she asks, out of habit.

    “Always.”

    Lena walks carefully by her side, her footfalls soundless and graceful as they follow the path of light. Her midnight evening gown swirls around her like clouds of smoke, trailing behind her in delicate rings. Her ivory skin mimics the moonlight, and she turns to Kara with a gentle smile.

    They stroll arm in arm, the sun and the moon, a rare moment of peace allowed between them.

    They make their way into an immaculate garden, greeted by rows of tables all clothed in blinding white. The strings of lights are placed carefully overhead, with glittering, golden bulbs that create the perfect evening glow. The leaves on the trees wave in cheerful introduction, as a slight breeze rustles through the area.

    There is a pleasant sound of soft chattering and the easy sound of brass instruments as they stroll deeper into the garden. They are not the first to arrive, and slip in fairly unnoticed, much to Kara’s relief. She knows this night will be anything but calm, but she’s grateful for the few brief moments to get her bearings before it all explodes into chaos.

    “Does it all have to be so beautiful?” Kara asks, leaning close to Lena’s ear. “The lights, the garden, the sky. Even the weather is perfect. It’s insulting.”

    “Mm,” Lena replies, not committing either way. “And you haven’t even seen the food yet.”

    “Hmph,” Kara grunts. “I’m not eating anything.”

    “Probably wise,” Lena winks, nudging her with her arm. Kara is infinitely grateful that Lena is there by her side, even though she knows what it really means. Her eye catches another streak of gray in Lena’s hair, but she doesn’t comment. Lena stops walking and motions with her head toward Kara. “You look lovely, by the way. That dress -- it suits you.”

    Kara’s knees go weak at the compliment, the way they so often do when Lena adorns her with such affection. Before she can respond with a few choice descriptions of her own, they’re interrupted by a voice.

    It calls out from somewhere close behind them, and it’s rich and sweet like golden honey. Kara finds herself leaning into it, immediately captivated, like it’s calling out to her specifically. It comes together in a crescendo of doves wings, and Kara is sure that the owner of such a voice must have a face like the angels she has gotten to know only in her dreams.

    “Hello Hades,” the voice says. They both turn in the direction of the sound and Kara is almost blinded by the sheer beauty in front of her.

    “So good to see you,” Lena replies, her voice carrying the same tone.

    “It’s been far too long,” the dynamic stranger practically sings. “And this must be Persephone. It’s lovely to finally put a face to the name.”

    Kara watches as the woman dips her head graciously. The lines in her neck elongate as her lips part in a genial smile. Kara extends her hand dumbly.

    “Hi,” she croaks, wincing at the sharp ugliness of her own voice in comparison to the goddess in front of her. Their eyes meet and Kara is struck in the heart as if by lightning. She looks at the magnificent stranger, and back to Lena. The woman’s eyes sparkle with familiar flecks of gold as she watches Kara with ease. Her hair is the same midnight black, her skin as white as porcelain. Her features seem to combine the starlight from the heavens, and the sheer magnificence of the Underworld.

    Kara remembers what it felt like to see Lena for the first time, and she feels like her heart is going to explode out of her chest.

    Lena doesn’t seem fazed by the stranger, though she’s equally as riveted by her presence. Kara can feel herself staring open-mouthed between the two, but she doesn’t know what to think right now.

    It’s an absolute marvel.

    She feels like she’s just discovered the best kept secret in the universe. There isn’t just one goddess of death, but there are two .

    “I won’t interrupt, I just wanted the pleasure of your acquaintance,” the stranger says, excusing herself. “So good to see you again, darling Hades.”

    Lena nods, quietly. They both stare as she walks away.

    Kara can feel Lena’s eyes shift to her, but she feels rooted to the spot, completely transfixed by what she just witnessed.

    “That was Aphrodite,” Lena’s explains softly as the identical immortal glides away. Kara notes the way Lena’s cheeks flush an attractive crimson. Kara looks once more between the two, trying to solve the puzzle quickly forming in her mind. “The Goddess of beauty.”

    “So they say,” Kara hums. The resemblance is uncanny. It’s downright unbelievable. Every feature, every mannerism, perfectly identical to the handsome goddess of Death she so adores. “But-- but she’s-- you?”

    Lena startles, her eyes widening briefly before a knowing smile passes over her face.

    “Beauty is in the eye of the beholder, Kara,” Lena explains. “Aphrodite transforms herself into what we perceive to be the most beautiful, the most appealing. It’s a true reflection of our heart’s desire, shown to us through her image. Such is her power.”

    Lena’s explanation takes a moment to settle in Kara’s chest. Aphrodite looks exactly like Lena, because of course she does. As far as Kara is concerned, there is no truer representation of beauty in all the cosmos.

    “She doesn’t look the same to everyone,” Lena clarifies, though it isn’t entirely necessary.

    “What does she look like to you?” Kara finally whispers, her throat noticeably dry.

    Lena’s eyes soften, and Kara knows she understands. She glances off after where Aphrodite has wandered with a thoughtful smile.

    “Do you even have to ask, darling?”

    Kara leans forward and presses her forehead against Lena’s, feeling the coolness of her skin and centering herself to the rhythm of her heart. She closes her eyes, and for one brief, glorious second, they’re far away from everyone else.

    “I need you to promise me something,” Lena says, her tone turning suddenly serious and almost lethal. Kara shivers, but doesn’t try to separate herself. Instead she just presses into Lena’s forehead a little harder. “If I ask you to do something later, promise me you’ll do it, without asking questions.”

    “Lena, I--” Kara begins, faltering. She doesn’t understand, and she knows she isn’t meant to. “I don’t know if I can do that.”

    “I need you trust me, even with all that’s going on, and all I’ve done,” Lena explains, practically begging. It’s nerve-wracking to hear her so desperate, but Kara simply holds her ground. “Can you do that?”

    “Of course,” Kara agrees, closing her eyes and trying to imagine what Lena could possibly need her to do. “Yes, I can do that.”

    “I promise, you’ll be okay. It will all be okay,” Lena says. “You have all of my protection.”

    “But what about you?”

    “Well isn’t this touching!”

    A long, menacing shadow gets cast over them, sweeping in quickly and stabbing through the center of the light. Kara’s neck snaps back as she turns to face the thunderous voice of her sworn enemy.

    “Lena! You’re looking… lively,” Lex announces, strolling casually toward them, replacing a watch into his pocket. His white linen suit flutters slightly in the breeze, but all Kara can seem to notice is the deep, midnight black of the shirt underneath. The fabric swirls like a living constellation on his chest, the same shade has Lena’s dress. The colors of death. “And Kara! My, my, it’s been far too long. You don’t look as tan as I remember. Must be a trick of the light.”

    Kara’s muscles flex involuntarily as she cranes her neck and tries to keep her composure. She knows striking out against Lex wouldn’t be the best idea, despite the ache in very soul telling her to go for it.

    “Another over the top affair,” Lena says, raising a pointed eyebrow in Lex’s direction. She immediately changes from warm and soft to ruthless and cold in the blink of an eye. Kara is impressed with the transformation, if not slightly rattled. “If ruling the cosmos doesn’t work, it’s nice to know that you have a fall back plan as a party planner.”

    “You think so little of me, Lena, and frankly - it hurts,” Lex touches his chest with a pout. Kara feels the heat of rage simmering in her chest. “You know me, I’m a sentimental guy. I didn’t do all of this --” he gestures grandly at the decor, “--for me. I did it for us.”

    “For us,” Lena repeats. She crosses her arms and stares at him in amusement. “How sweet.”

    “Do you remember when we were younger?” Lex sidles up alongside the pair and takes a long sip of his drink. He snakes his arm around Lena’s shoulders while directing his stare at Kara. “My sister is the real sentimental one. I suppose it’s rubbed off on me, now. But she was always so fascinated by power, so engrossed by everything I was doing, completely adoring of her big brother. It was kind of endearing, if not a little tragic. Any time I’d go anywhere, she would wait up for me. For hours, days, just waiting for me to return. You know, no matter what, it’s something I could always count on. My loyal little sister, always by my side. Even now, with worlds between us, I can always count on my sister to be there.”

    “You don’t deserve-- ” Kara spits, before Lex interjects.

    “In a way, you can look at this party as a thank you,” Lex grins, ignoring Kara completely and talking over her. “Welcome back, my dear sister.”

    Kara goes to move forward, but Lena gently tugs on her arm.

    “Don’t,” she whispers. Kara freezes.

    “Don’t take it personally,” Lex gloats, pulling Lena closer to his side. He has maneuvered so the they are standing apart from Kara now, a noticeable divide. “It’s a family thing. You wouldn’t understand.”

    “If you hadn’t destroyed my home--” Kara snarls, stepping forward. Her mind is whirling, and all her carefully calculated plans for how this encounter should go are violently tossed aside. Lex holds up his hand stares at her, smiling . Kara watches the way he doesn’t seem threatened in the least, and in fact looks to be enjoying himself. She tries to make eye contact with Lena, to implore her to do something, but she avoids her stare. She simply stands next to Lex, allowing for it all to happen.

    Kara wonders if this is what it was like, all those years ago, when the Titans were facing their demise. The sister of the beast, standing obediently by his side. Then, everything starts to come into focus.

    “Lena?” Kara whimpers. “What’s going on?”

    “Now I’d love to stay and chat, but really, I do want to get on with things, don’t you?” Lex asks, turning toward his sister.

    “I’m sorry, Kara,” Lena says simply. Kara swears she can hear a sniffle as Lena turns away from her.

    “Lena, what are you doing? Where are you going?” Kara takes a step and tries to reach out, but Lex steps in between them.

    “You’re more than welcome to join her,” Lex replies, his smile gleaming in the moonlight. “I would never turn that down. Two for the price of one, such a bargain.”

    “You got what you wanted, as we agreed,” Lena replies cooly. She turns and faces Kara once more, her eyes swirling with tears. “Kara, please. I need you to go home.”

    “Well, do enjoy the festivities first,” Lex insists. He points overhead. “There’s going to be quite the fireworks display later.”

    “I thought--” Kara frowns. “But I’m here, just as you asked. This is what you wanted.”

    “Originally, yes, that was the plan,” Lex scratches along his chin, grinning wickedly. “But it seems our dear Hades here had some other ideas. I have to admit, she made me a compelling offer, one I would be remiss to pass up. Turns out I won’t be requiring your services after all. You’re free to go.”

    They both turn away, and Kara hears Lex whispering in Lena’s ear, “I’m going to make you regret this more than you already do.”

    “So you’re-- what? Going to take Lena and tie her up somewhere on Olympus?” Kara tries to bait him. He pauses, before the sickening sound of his laughter fills her ears. He turns back and approaches her, close enough so that his thick, hot breath trails along her face.

    “Puppets don’t need to be tied up, Kara,” Lex says calmly. He pulls Lena in closer, jostling her arm with excessive force. Kara feels the electricity build in her veins. “You just hang them up by their strings.”

    “Why did you ask Lena to bring me here?” Kara asks, using her one last attempt to understand. The tears well up behind her eyes, and she wishes with everything she has to keep it together. At least for a few minutes longer. She does not want to cry in front of this monster. “What was the point? You already got what you wanted.”

    “Oh, no, Kara, that’s where you’re wrong,” Lex says, flashing her a wicked smile. “What I really wanted was to look into your eyes the moment you lost everything,” Lex shrugs, adjusting the ring on his finger. His eyes go red with a volatile heat as he smiles at Kara again. “And I have to say, it’s been well worth the wait.”

    “Go home, Kara,” Lena insists, glancing back over her shoulder. Her words are muffled by the tears she’s trying to keep back. “You promised you’d listen to me.”

    Before she can argue, Lex pulls Lena away, dragging her along violently.

    “Lena!” Kara cries out, but her words echo against nothing, lost to the swirl of darkness. The pair have already disappeared into the night.

    “LENA!”
