    The Underworld seems to have transformed overnight, turning downright frigid, the landscape a treacherous maze of sneaky black ice. The wind stings with more bite today, Cat thinks, as she glides along the well-worn path to the village, huddling tightly against the relentless whips of air. She can see little whispery puffs of breath in front of her as she exhales, a small sign of her spiritual exertion. It’s the only thing she can really see clearly, as it seems the entire realm has been plunged into an endless darkness. The hazy fog has been replaced by a cloak of night, the crags and edges of the kingdom hidden away from view entirely. It always gets like this when Lena leaves the Underworld: a little darker, a little colder, but this time feels different. The winter seems harsher, more permanent. Cat shivers at the thought, pushing away the discomfort in her chest as she picks up her pace.

    She knows there is something different going on - she felt it as soon as Lena returned from Olympus. There was something the goddess of death wasn’t telling them, and whatever it was, it felt bigger than a slight omission. Cat mutters to herself as she curses Lena’s bad habit of trying to protect everyone and how every time she does she puts herself in danger. It has happened more times than Cat cares to remember, but each time, Lena returns a little worse for wear. But this, this is new. This feels more serious than all the other times Lena has gone out on a limb. The entire fabric of the Underworld has shifted, and everything feels like it has been frozen in time just waiting for the signal to be released.

    The unmistakable sound of footsteps shakes her out of her thoughts as they echo in the silence behind her. The rhythmic click-clacking is emphasized by the cavernous landscape, making it impossible to disguise. They are fast approaching, with a confident footstrike that feels out of place as it gains on her heels. Cat pauses her movements as she contemplates turning around. 

    The sounds cease.

    “Odd,” Cat remarks, to no one in particular. It is not like Lena to trail behind, or even play a joke, so Cat squares her jaw as she contemplates what else it could be. Kara isn’t stealthy enough, despite her best intentions, and the idea of her trying to sneak around in the dark brings a small smile to Cat’s face. She chances a quick glance from side to side, but nothing moves. The darkness remains still as death. She sighs. Maybe she’s finally teetering on the edge of sanity. It’s been a long time since she’s relaxed -- centuries, it seems -- and maybe all of the stress is finally catching up with her. She squares her shoulders in an effort to reset before she continues her trek back home.

    The footsteps continue as soon as she begins to move again. She glides a bit faster, careful not to disrupt any of the unruly, hidden rocks underfoot, but the sound seems to match her cadence. She then slows down to a leisurely pace, holding her breath as she listens to the way the footsteps ease in time with her own.

    “Kara, you’re not going to fool me, and if you think this is a good use of time--,” Cat begins, before a huge gust of wind blows her clear off her feet. It howls with a ghastly wail, a sound that creaks and cracks against her ears. She resists the gust, frowning, as if insulted by the wind’s audacity. 

    “Show yourself!” Cat demands, whirling around with a pointed finger. A useless weapon to the untrained eye, but Cat has always preferred words to swords. “Only cowards hide in the dark!”

    There is dead silence for several seconds, before a long, angular shadow is cast before her, blacker than even the deadest of night. Cat blinks, startled, as a tall, dark figure slithers from the depths, the smoke coiling as it places itself at her feet. She can feel her knees tremble as she stares up into orange eyes and a devilish face that holds a gleaming smile.

    “You--,” Cat starts, before shaking her head fiercely. “Impossible.”

    Lillian rolls her eyes, glancing around the Underworld with a look of smug satisfaction. She shrugs her shoulders as she grins back at Cat, teasing her with her nonchalance. “Come now, nothing is impossible for an immortal.”

    “You’re--,” Cat begins, her outstretched arm falling to her side as she tries to control the surprise in her voice. She shakes her head, quieting her nerves as she glares in the demon’s direction. “Well, frankly, I’m a little surprised to see you here.”

    The demon in front of her looks familiar, but it isn’t just her appearance that gives her away: it’s the feeling Cat gets when standing in her presence. It’s like returning to the darkest corners of her most treacherous nightmares. She feels waves of heat roll through her body, tempered by shocking ice, the sensations both unpleasant and nearly unbearable. Only the strongest immortals can procure such a feeling in the darkest depths of the Underworld. 

    The demon’s eyes swirl as she studies Cat harshly, and the way her eyebrow juts skyward exposes her identity. Cat has never seen her before in the flesh, but somehow the family resemblance is uncanny. Lena had trusted her enough to impart at least a little intimate knowledge about her family, and Cat was aware that Lillian existed somewhere deep in the depths of the Underworld as a prisoner. But to see her now, standing in front of her, and inexplicably free, is enough to render even Cat Grant momentarily speechless.

    “Ah yes, Cat Grant, as I live and breathe,” Lillian steps forward, staring her down with disgust. “I suppose that’s more than I can say for you though, isn’t it?”

    “A wasted life in a prison is not a life at all,” Cat retorts, finding her fire even in the face of the most evil. She’s holding her own against the infamous demon, the mother of the most powerful beings in the cosmos, her pride refusing to let her win. “Even for an immortal, or whatever it is you call yourself these days. I lost track after the first iteration.”

    “It’s nice to see you haven’t lost your way with words,” Lillian chides, stepping dangerously close to Cat’s trembling form. “I can tell my daughter has regaled you with her familial tales of woe,” Lillian drawls, gesturing lazily. “But I should warn you, she has a certain flair for the dramatic. It would be wise not to believe everything she says.”

    “I can see where she gets it,” Cat remarks automatically, without thinking. She clenches her jaw, unblinking. “Now, what are you doing here?”

    Lillian sneers before tutting her lips, as if to pity Cat’s simple mind. The rage churns in her chest as she waits for the demon’s next reply. “While you’ve been incapable of keeping Lena under surveillance, I have been summoned to take over.”

    “Right,” Cat scoffs. “She just let you waltz right out of Tartarous--,” she stops speaking at the way Lillian silently challenges her. “You-- she-- she let you out of Tartarous? On purpose?”

    “Move aside,” Lillian says sharply. “I don’t have time for simple games. I am here to help my daughter.”

    “Like Hades you are,” Cat seethes, inserting herself back into Lillian’s path. She knows the relationship between Lillian and Lena is complicated at best, but she finds it extremely hard to believe that Lena would just let her mother roam free without telling anyone. But then again, the only person powerful enough to release a prisoner from the depths of Tartarous would be the ruler herself.

    But why ?

    “It must be hard, to be cast aside like you’re worthless,” Lillian says, reading the confusion on Cat’s face. “Don’t take it personally. My daughter gets bored easily and loves going after shiny new things.”

    “What do you want, demon? I am much too busy to be listening to your cryptic ramblings.”

    Lillian chuckles at that, the sound smoky and hot, like Cat would imagine the center of Tartarous to be. She pictures a land filled with fire and brimstone and bubbling, oozing lava. She’s never attempted to venture there, despite her insatiable curiosity, because Lena has always gone out of her way to warn her off. Despite the fact that Cat gets a certain joy out of teasing the goddess of Death, she doesn’t dare disobey when her eyes swirl with darkness and her jaw sets permanently like sculpted marble. When Lena speaks with a haunted voice, and her entire being casts an impenetrable shadow, even Cat listens.

    “Ah, yes, I’m sure Lena has given you plenty to do in her absence,” Lillian smirks, crossing her arms in challenge. 

    Cat deflates at that slightly, since it’s becoming increasingly clearer that she has been left in the dark, literally and figuratively. She doesn’t know Lena’s plans, and the fact that her mother seems more privy to this information is irksome, to say the least. 

    Lillian recognizes the weakness and all but launches at it. “Lena hasn’t really trusted you, in all these years, has she? She’s cunning, my daughter, no matter what she might have you believe. Do you even know where she is right now, or what she’s doing?”

    Something deep inside Cat erupts suddenly, causing her to launch herself at Lillian. She forgets who she is, and what she is -- all she can see is fire. But when she lunges, she flies right through the shadows, and her entire soul vibrates with the sound of heavy laughter. Lillian turns to her with amusement, shrugging as if the entire thing is a childish amusement. Cat straightens herself and takes a deep breath, before facing Lillian’s sharply raised eyebrow.

    “If you’re done with the theatrics, I’m going to Earth, so I can undo the wretched mess my daughter has put us in. I suggest you join me, and gather the rest of that horrid village, before the Underworld becomes even more unbearable than it is now.”

    Cat scoffs, rolling her eyes. “I’m going to take orders from you.” It isn’t a question but there is still a faint taste of disbelief as the words leave her tongue. 

    “For once, we want the same thing,” Lillian says, her tone shifting slightly to something almost soft. 

    Cat wouldn’t call it gentle by any means, but the venom behind her words seems to have subsided for the moment. She’s unsettled, and her eyes dart around cautiously. Cat realizes she’s startled, and the thought is unnerving. 

    “If you care about my daughter at all, you’ll listen to me.”

    “Why would you be helping her? After everything--,” Cat hesitates, contemplating. She knows this is a trick, but she has to tread lightly if she wants to make any headway. Lena is the reason her mother has been locked away for centuries, and to think that her freedom doesn’t come at a price would be foolish.

    “You see it, I know you do, even with your tragically ordinary eyes,” Lillian interjects wisely, and the implication sends a shiver down Cat’s spine. “She’s slower these days. She walks with a hunch, her breath comes in fits and starts. You’ve seen the lines etched along her face. It’s not your imagination.”

    “No--,” Cat starts, but something ties her words up in knots. She thinks of Lena’s face the last time she saw her, with its sallow color that seemed worn and tired, replacing the flawless marble that used to glow with effervescent beauty. She remembers the way her smile was slow and pained, her eyes dead and dark. The unbreakable goddess seemed fragile in more ways than one. Cat bites her lip to keep from crying out. Instead, she swallows the lump in her throat and whispers almost inaudibly. “It can’t be.”

    “I assure you, it is, and this is not the time for your foolish pride to get in the way,” Lillian says, exasperated. “Lena is in trouble, and it would really speed things along if you would join the cause.”

    “What have you done to her?” Cat asks, taking another step into Lillian’s space. 

    “When it comes to finding trouble, Lena doesn’t need my help,” Lillian scoffs, holding her hand up to stop Cat in her tracks. “I couldn’t have set this up better if I tried.”

    A blast from above shakes the Underworld to its core, cracking a jagged line through the ground that extends for miles. Cat and Lillian both stumble, clawing at the ice to try to steady themselves. The way Lillian’s eyes widen in panic, however briefly, before she slips into her casual snarl, gives Cat the push she needs to make her decision.

    “I don’t know what you’re planning, but I’m listening,” says Cat as she slowly finds her footing again. Suddenly, a glowing yellow light stabs through the darkness from above, illuminating the ground floor of the Underworld, calling to them like a beacon. Cat shields her eyes, staring in the direction the light is coming from. 

    Never, in all her years in the realm of Hades, has she seen this kind of light down here. She immediately fears for Lena’s life. 

    Lillian whispers in her ear to rally the dead, and without a second’s hesitation, Cat flies off to the village. The yellow light grows stronger, more powerful, and Lillian angles her face to the source, a slow, easy smile on her lips as she allows it to consume her.

    Kara stands in the middle of Zeus’ sprawling garden, her entire body engulfed in white hot flames. She feels the fiery spirit of the Underworld coursing through her veins as she tries to formulate a plan. The gods and goddesses of Zeus have all departed, and she is alone, casting a trailing light down to the depths and up to the heavens, strong enough for the entire cosmos to follow. It isn’t even something she consciously tries to do, but the light flows through her as bright and strong as her belief in the goddess that’s been taken.  

    She has to find Lena before it’s too late. 

    She closes her eyes, picturing Lena’s flawless face, the flowing river of her easy smile when times were better. She feels another jolt of light extend through her fingertips, and above the crown of her head, but she remains steady. The memory of Lena’s laugh, melodic and rich, sends a jolt through Kara’s core, and she feels the sunlight radiating directly from her chest. She opens her eyes slowly and they immediately adjust to the bright explosion of light she’s created. It doesn’t take long before she notices a small, dark portal in front of her. She frowns, taking a small step forward, before the entire Earth begins to rumble and quake. With a pause, she watches as hundreds of thousands of spirits begin rushing through the door, chanting and shouting the praises of their lost Queen. 

    “Spirits!” Kara cries out, holding her arms out. She isn’t sure whether to weep for joy, or panic at their release. “What are you doing here?”

    “To save the Queen! To save Hades!” They all rhythmically chant, and Kara exhales in relief. She watches as an endless line of spirits: old, young, bright and dim all swirl through the portal and surround her. 

    A familiar presence appears by her side and her body relaxes slightly.

    “You rang?” Cat’s voice greets her ears, and Kara can’t help the smile that appears on her face.

    “Cat!” she exclaims, turning to face her friend. She practically throws her arms around the spirit, despite the fact that she is merely a whisper in the wind. “You came! You’re here! But how--how did you do it?”

    “You wouldn’t believe me if I told you,” Cat says, and Kara immediately gets the feeling that she’s right. “Where is she?”

    “He’s got her--,” Kara says, her lips trembling as she is forced to say it out loud. “They went off, he dragged her away. She’s gone.”

    “Then you have to find a way to bring her back!” Cat commands.

    In the distance, a rumble of thunder shakes the ground, getting louder and louder as if the sound had been placed permanently above them. Kara watches in astonishment as a horde of dark, angry shadows begin to appear over the hill, one after the other, gathering in speed as they descend upon the garden. Cat glances at her with narrowed eyes as they freeze, waiting. The chain of demons seem infinite, angrily rushing toward them with gnashing teeth and wild eyes. The spirits of the Underworld immediately change direction, creating a wall of impenetrable spirits to greet Zeus’ weapons.

    Cat immediately begins to head toward the threat. 

    “What are you doing?” Kara cries out after her. 

    “Helping you, of course!” Cat shouts, dodging her arms and rushing past her. She directs several spirits to begin assembling across the lawn to hold off Zeus’ army of minions. “Now go! We’ll handle this, you go find Lena! Hurry!”

    Kara nods, feeling uplifted by the aid of the spirits of the Underworld. They unlock another level of strength she didn’t know she possessed, and it gives her the courage to begin her search. She takes off into the night, rocketing high and powerful like a comet into the sky. The Earth quickly falls away as she tunes all her senses and attention to finding Lena. 

    Cat, momentarily distracted by Kara's grand exit, pauses. "That," she contemplates, looking up into the sky, "really is the coolest thing I've ever seen."

    She thinks about it briefly with a small smile, before a stumbling spirit bumps into her side. "Hageus, for Hades' sake! You're going to get us all re-killed. Get over there!"

    Kara doesn’t hold back, propelling herself higher and faster than normal. There’s no telling where Lex would stash Lena, since it’s not something she’s stopped to consider before now. All this time, she assumed Lex would be coming for her, that the plan would be to turn Kara into his own weapon of destruction. But now that this has turned dangerously personal, she wishes she knew more about Lex to understand the complicated dynamics between him and his sister. She wonders if he means to gloat, or if he will hide her away in a place no one -- not even a Titan -- can hope to enter.

    It's maddening to think about and she surges forward with tight jawed determination before a memory plows into her chest full force and steals the breath from her lungs. She remembers the soft touch of Lena’s gentle hands, and the warmth of her lips when they trace her own, and her entire mind clears. As fast as it comes, all the anxiety vanishes. Even in times of peril, Lena finds a way to help her. She closes her eyes and hones in on the only sound that matters now: a steady pounding drum that beats only for her.

    It takes a few minutes, and it’s fainter than normal -- a sign of weakness that makes Kara’s muscles tense -- but it’s there. In an instant, Kara knows where to go. 

    A fluttering sound of wings interrupts her thoughts and she spots Winn flying in her periphery. 

    “This way, follow me!” He exclaims, rushing past her with little explanation. Kara clenches her jaw and shoots forward, trying to keep the tricky little god in her sights as they bolt through the sky.

    The pair expertly dodge clouds and birds of all kinds as they head toward the mountain, and Kara knows immediately they are heading for Olympus. An obvious choice, in some respects, but a baffling one in others. It isn’t exactly hidden, but Kara doesn’t try to decode Lex’s intentions. She simply listens as Lena’s heartbeat continues to thump steadily in her ears. 

    “They haven’t left yet!” Winn calls out, as if reading Kara’s thoughts. “There’s still time!”

    “Where will he take her after this?” Kara shouts, but Winn simply shrugs and picks up the pace once more.

    They land on the steps of the palace, but before Kara can burst through the doors, Winn grabs her arm.

    “Quiet!” He orders. His face is stern, which looks awkward on his usual cheerful cheeks. “You can’t barge in there or you’ll ruin everything. You have to wait. Be stealthy.”

    “I can’t just stall --,” Kara begins to argue, but she’s interrupted by the booming sound of thunderous laughter coming from above them. “I’m going in!”

    “Just stay hidden!” Winn hisses. “For everyone’s sake!”

    Kara rolls her eyes, but moves quietly, just in case there is more to the warning than Winn is letting on. They tip-toe through the great hall, following the sound of voices that Kara can only pray truly belong to Lex and Lena. It wouldn’t be the first time she’s been fooled by the pair of them, and the thought settles deep and uncomfortably in her stomach.

    The marbled floors are polished to perfection, and she catches a glimpse of her own face in the spectacular veneer. Her eyebrows are knit together in desperation, but she looks strong, intimidating even. She wonders when she started to look so different, and how long it’s been since she’s seen in her own reflection. Before she can really go down that road, Winn is ushering her around the corner. 

    “Listen,” he commands, and Kara stiffens.

    “You won’t have to go through the painstaking process of making me comfortable,” Kara hears Lena scoff, and her heart pounds heavily in her chest. “We both know I don’t have much time.”

    “Somehow, you’re even more morbid than before, tell me, how do you do it?” Lex chuckles, and the rage burns itself on Kara’s cheeks. “You’ll at least get to see how this ends, I suspect. Then you can spend the last of your mortal days making it up to me.”

    “She’s--,” Kara yelps, immediately placing a hand to her mouth. She lowers her voice to a whisper. “She’s mortal! But how?”

    “She traded herself for you,” Winn shrugs. “An even trade, if you think about it.”

    Kara swats him, harder than intended, and he looks at her with wide eyes. “I’m only kidding.”

    “I’m going in,” Kara tells him, shifting by the door and bracing to disrupt whatever it is Lex is planning next. Winn grabs her arm.

    “No!” he exclaims. “No. You have to stay here. You’ll lose her forever if you don’t listen! Besides--” He places a warning hand on her shoulder. “You can’t turn her back. It’s done.”

    “How do you know that?” Kara asks, but as usual, Winn only shrugs. An infuriating thing, the flaky god of flight.

    “Stop looking at me like that. Lovely Lena, always the victim,” Lex drawls, his tone condescending. “If you had just left well enough alone, you wouldn’t be in this mess.”

    “You knew I wouldn’t be able to stay out of it,” Lena argues. “Once you went after Kara…”

    “No, you have a very bad habit of making your weaknesses painfully obvious,” Lex interrupts loudly. He clenches his jaw and Kara notices the way his eyes blaze. “It isn’t even a challenge anymore, Lena. You’re only lucky it’s me who exploited it and not someone else, then we’d really be in trouble, hm?”

    Kara feels her body tremble with anger as she angles herself closer. She feels the heat, hot and electric, hum through her body as she watches the way Lex smiles at his own perceived brilliance. He takes another step closer and places a hand on Lena’s shoulder.

    “You know, Lena, it isn’t all your fault. I may have come from poison, but you somehow came from love, and if the rest of this family stands steadily in the darkness, you will always fall into the light. Even amongst the dregs of the dead,” Lex sighs, shaking his head with a small scoff. “It’s why it had to be you. It could never be anyone else.”

    “Touching,” Lena says, shrugging out of his grasp. “It’s certainly doing wonders for me now.”

    “Oh, darling sister, Kara will come after you soon enough,” Lex glances at his watch with an amused smile. “Then the real party can begin.”

    Winn chances a glance at Kara before she pushes him aside.

    The turmoil surrounding the garden of Zeus brings a kind of unbridled joy that Lillian thought dead and gone from her painfully infinite life. But within the chaos, amongst a backdrop of howling dead spirits ripping into the flesh of her son’s otherworldly weapons, Lillian finds clarity. She closes her eyes with a satisfied smile, taking a second to savor the moment that she helped create. The battle between her children has been a long time in coming, and she has always planned to have a front row seat to the show. It’s hard to pick sides, but this time, she’s going to do it right. Her son is a master manipulator, and his brilliance is terrifying, but his arrogance has proven costly in the past. Her daughter, on the other hand, could be great . She has her flaws, it’s true, and to be so despicably desperate, to be so easily convinced, it gives Lillian pause on who she should ultimately choose. But in the meantime, regardless of her children and their shortcomings, everything they’ve gone through has been worthwhile for this .

    A spirit howls in agony as her son’s demons rip it to pieces with a single slice, and Lillian nods approvingly.

    But they aren’t done yet -- not by a long shot. There is still work to be done if all her plans are to come to fruition. She opens her eyes and turns to continue surveying. She nods stiffly at Cat, who is dutifully directing traffic as the dead try to hold off Lex’s army. It’s curious, the way one of Lena’s subjects feels so loyal to her that they don’t even ask questions, choosing instead to follow blindly into battle. It’s more curious, still, that the entire Underworld is compelled to fight for her, despite the fact that she has kept them all tragically mortal , but Lillian doesn’t waste time trying to understand that.

    Lena has always been too sentimental, too soft for her own good, and it’s the reason she has never been able to outsmart her brother without significant assistance.

    It’s also the reason she is the goddess to be feared above all others.  And this time, Lillian promises herself, it will be different.

    With Cat distracted, and Kara nowhere to be found, Lillian snaps her fingers and leaves the cathartic scene of war behind. Within seconds, she appears in front of the holding cell for the most interesting criminal she’s ever had the pleasure of visiting.

    Sam Arias sits in a corner of the cell, her feet flat on the floor as her long legs angle close to her huddled body. She has them pulled up to her chest as she clutches them for support, her head resting on the top of her knees. Her brown hair curls languidly around her face, covering her eyes.

    She feels the woman’s presence outside of her cell before she sees her, but it isn’t enough to get her to lift her head. If it isn’t the guard telling her she’s free, or Alex coming to beg for forgiveness, Sam has decided she’s not interested. 

    Lillian’s first impression of the woman in the cell is that she’s structurally sound, but the way she’s slumped over makes her look defeated. Her second thought is that this simply won’t do. 

    “Giving up already, are we?” Lillian criticizes, without introduction. She straightens the lapels of her black trench coat, smoothing the lines to make sure she appears perfectly ordinary. It has been close to a millennium since she’s ventured to Earth and donned an Earthly disguise, and it feels foreign in ways she can’t let Sam notice quite yet. 

    Sam’s head slowly raises as she eyes the woman in front of her with mild curiosity. “Who are you?”

    Her voice is ordinary, mortal, but her eyes are deep, dark and endless. Lillian grins. 

    “No time for that, dear,” Lillian flutters her hand, granting herself access to the cell by slipping through the bars as if by magic. Sam’s eyes widen as she pushes herself further against the wall. “I’m on a schedule.”

    “How did you--what are--,” Sam stammers, trying to keep the distance between them. “Stay back!”

    “I’m not here to hurt you,” Lillian raises her arms to show her lack of weapons. “Far from it, in fact. I’m here because I need you. The world needs you.”

    “You need me? I don’t even know you--,” Sam argues, crossing her arms against her chest. “I can’t help anyone. Go away.”

    “Defeat doesn’t look good on you, dear,” Lillian replies, rolling her eyes. She eyes the cot in the corner with disgust, then shakes her head and sits down on it gently. “You are so much more than you know.”

    Sam shrugs, wiping away a rogue tear that’s escaped down her cheek. “What do you want?” 

    “I need you to attack Supergirl,” Lillian says casually, as if she’s delivering the weather report. 

    “What are you talking about--”

    Lillian rolls her eyes. “I know you’re a part time human, but please try to keep up. You’re one of the most powerful weapons in the universe and I need you to do what you’ve been designed to do. And I happen to know that it’s Supergirl you want.”

    “Weapon? Supergirl? Lady, I don’t know who you are or what you think you’re doing, but I’m not what you think I am. I’m no one. You’re making a mistake.”

    Sam turns her head away from the woman, hoping against hope that she will just disappear back where she came from. She doesn’t know what’s happening, or why everyone keeps looking at her with suspicious eyes. She just wants to go home and go to sleep. And when she wakes up, she’d like for all of this to be over. 

    “Your girlfriend brought you here on suspicion of being linked to Reign, did she not?” Lillian accuses, and Sam swallows heavily. She thinks of Alex, and the way her eyes watered as she placed the handcuffs around Sam’s wrists. It burns to think of her, even when she almost understands, because this isn’t how it should be happening. Alex hasn’t said it yet, but she doesn’t have to, her hesitant eyes and trembling lips said it all loud and clear. She thinks Sam is Reign, and it would be laughable if it wasn’t so scary. 

    How could she be a masked terrorist living in the shadows without any idea that she’s involved? 

    Lillian continues, “You have a lot of lost time to account for, don’t you, Samantha?”

    “I--,” Sam stumbles. The truth about her memory lapse hangs between them like smoke, and Sam grimaces. She turns back to face the stranger, frowning. “How do you know all of this?”

    “You are meant to cleanse the world of false idols, to purge the planet of sin,” Lillian recites, watching the way the muscles in Sam’s jaw clench and her neck stiffens as the words sink in. “The people of Earth worship her like a god, and she is not . You must destroy Supergirl, restore the balance once more.”

    The words seems to awaken something deep in Sam’s chest. She feels a fiery rage begin to burn, and she hears a long, rumbling shout before everything fades to black.

    Lillian watches the switch, relishing in the way Sam slumps over only for Reign to fully engulf her soul. She watches her eyes open with wide-eyed anger, and her shoulders pull back with colossal strength. She stands from the ground slowly, her legs long and lithe, her arms sculpted by magic of the oldest order. She stares through Lillian like she doesn’t even see her, and begins to speak. 

    “I will destroy her,” Reign’s booming voice echoes out over the room, and it sends a pleasing chill down to Lillian’s feet. 

    “That’s better,” Lillian nods, studying the figure in front of her. She’s tall, and strong, and a perfect equal to Kara’s immeasurable power. Reign’s eyes glow an immortal red, behind an impenetrable mask of black. It’s more pleasing to witness up close than Lillian even expected.

    She turns on her heel and beckons. “Yes, this will do nicely. Follow me.”

    Kara has taken to pacing the hallways of Olympus, contemplating her next move, as Winn flutters behind, urging her not to do anything rash. But she can’t focus, can’t think, can’t even function, beyond visions of saving Lena. She sees herself busting through the door faster than Lex can react, grabbing Lena as she brands him with a laser stare. She pictures herself shielding Lena from harm and deflecting Lex’s thunderbolts, threatening to use it against him unless he returns Lena’s power. 

    “She’s not yours!” Kara would shout, if given the chance. Lena isn’t any of theirs, not even hers. She doesn’t belong to any realm, because she is beyond any of the gods’ power. 

    Scenario after scenario flash before her, each one more heroic than the last, but none of them satisfying enough to be real . She’s sure that the anguish and rage she feels now is enough to send Olympus burning to the ground with little effort, and she sees it as if in a vision: the entire Kingdom ignited, the palace destroyed in a hurricane of fiery flames. It makes her almost delirious with power. She knows it’s wrong, but there’s a large part of her that can’t help but lean into the fantasy just a bit. After all, there’s no part of Olympus that feels like home to her. It would be a triumphant victory to watch it crumble. 

    The only thing that keeps her from acting is the fact that it’s all deceptively easy. 

    “Too easy,” she thinks, and it weighs down on her shoulders enough to keep her grounded. There’s no way Lex, who has been a step ahead of her since she was born, would allow her to walk right up and destroy Mount Olympus without a defense. Unless he wanted her to. 

    And the last thing she’s going to do is something Lex wants. So she waits.

    Winn nudges alongside her. “Do you hear that?”

    Kara pauses, frowning. She hears nothing, not even a whisper. In fact, she can’t hear anything at all. It feels like she’s been pulled into a vacuum, void of any and all life. Even Lena’s heartbeat has been muted. “Hear what?”

    “The absence of something.”

    Kara strains, her ears listening for the slightest change in pitch, the tiniest intake of breath, but nothing comes.

    “It’s almost time,” Winn says, looking at her as if she should understand more than what he’s saying. “She’s here.”

    “Who--,” Kara starts to ask, before the entire castle is plunged into terrifying darkness.

    The black night smothers her heavily, choking the life out of her lungs. It feels clumsy and out of place, and no matter how hard she strains, she can’t seem to break through. She feels completely alone, isolated, and her chest begins to seize in panic. The breaths come short and fast, but none of them deep enough as she gasps for air.

    “To the one the Earth mortals worship as a god--” Reign’s terrifying voice rings out, shaking the walls of the palace. Kara freezes. “Show yourself, or they will all burn.”

    The lights flicker slightly, before a fuse blows, resulting in a low, dim area that exposes Kara’s position. She places herself outside the door where Lex and Lena were just standing, but she can’t see them anymore. All she can see is a long hallway, under threatening lights that seem to flicker and call for her. 

    It feels like her entire existence has brought her to this very moment: on the one hand, she desperately wants to pull Lena away from the clutches of her family, to save her once and for all. She wants to spend the rest of her days protecting the beautiful goddess of her dreams, no matter the cost. On the other, it seems her true purpose has finally been realized. She knows she has to face Reign if she’s going to have a chance to save everyone. The mortals have no idea what hangs in the balance, and Kara only hopes she can spare them from ever having to wonder. But beyond that, she knows the fate of the cosmos is also in her hands. The gods and Titans of the past have all chosen sides in order to create the ultimate face off. Kara only hopes she can make the right decision and see it through. 

    She takes a last look at the room where she knows Lena is still captive, and a tear falls down her face. Lena wouldn’t hesitate, and so Kara knows she must be brave. If she doesn’t step up and beat Reign, there may not be a world for her and Lena to share at all. 

    “I’ll be back for you,” Kara whispers, a promise she sends out into the universe in desperation of making it come true. “I promise.”

    With one final look, she leaves everything behind and walks outside the palace gates.

    Reign is standing ready to greet her, her eyes burning red as she watches Kara with calculated interest. Kara swallows heavily, doing everything she can to keep her mind clear and calm. She hears a thumping in her ears, in time with her footfalls, but she knows it isn’t her own heartbeat. She turns and looks up at the balcony. She expects it to be empty, but in case it’s not, she still takes a chance to catch a glimpse of Lena if she should be so fortunate. A flash of midnight black hair and moonlight skin presses anxiously against the window, and Kara’s chest fills with warmth. She exhales and offers a small, confident smile to the goddess above, who she knows won’t be able to see it. She hopes it’s enough for her to feel safe. 

    She turns back to Reign.

    “I’m here,” Kara says, her voice scratchy and low. She begins to slowly descend the stairs of the palace with her arms raised. “You don’t have to hurt anyone.”

    Reign smirks, as she looks up at Kara. Her eyes follow every movement, map every intake of breath. Kara allows herself to be dissected, piece by piece. When they’re finally face to face, Kara notes the difference in height -- Reign has a few inches on her -- but that’s the only obvious advantage. She appears more ordinary than Kara expects, but she keeps her guard up. Nothing is ever as it seems when it comes to the weapons of gods.

    “This world has sunken into chaos and sin,” Reign declares. “Too many have eluded judgement. I have been born to cleanse the scourge and deliver the awakening!”

    “You don’t have to do this--,”Kara steps forward, arms outstretched. She’s desperate to reach an understanding. “I am not here to pass judgment. I am only here to help.”

    “Ha! So full of hubris, like the Titans before you who feared my makers. They sat around worshipping false gods as they watched our planet suffocate by shame and burn from memory,” Reign’s lips curl in disgust. She raises her head, her chin pointing down at Kara. “Stand down, or I will make you join them in their purgatory.”

    “I can’t let you hurt anymore innocent people,” Kara pleads. “This isn’t right!” 

    “There is no innocence. There is only sin!” Reign shouts. 

    Without warning, she launches toward Kara.

    It feels like she’s flown directly into a cement truck as Reign barrels into her, knocking her clear off her feet. Kara recovers swiftly, taking off into the air and stopping the momentum mid-strike. She shoots herself forward and meets Reign again, her muscles flexed and ready for impact. Reign doesn’t even flinch as Kara lands a heavy blow to the side of her head. She snarls at the attempt, and retaliates with a punch of her own. Kara feels the throbbing pain as soon as Reign’s fist meets her face, but she grits her teeth and tries to hide her discomfort.

    For several agonizing minutes, Reign meets her blow for blow, and seems as strong and unbreakable as Kara herself. Kara feels the white hot heat pulsing inside her, burning with the power of the spirits. Despite the unexpected aid, she’s still only barely holding her own against Reign’s superior skill set.

    “Your queen is never coming back,” Reign sneers, launching a kick directly into Kara’s ribs. “You fight for nothing .”

    Kara slumps over slightly, caught off guard by the force in Reign’s kick. Suddenly, she’s airborne, locked in Reign’s grip as she flies them both to the roof of the castle.

    “We can help you--,” Kara huffs, trying to stand up again. Despite her shaky legs, she finds her footing, but Reign sends her sprawling with a back-handed slap that feels like a lightning bolt. Kara goes tumbling to the ground. Coughing for breath, Kara pulls herself on to her knees, where she inhales deeply for several seconds. 

    She remembers the way Reign looked on the monitor at CatCo when Kara first saw her: the cold, metallic sound to her voice and the deep, dark eyes. But when the screen froze, and everyone else was distracted, Kara knows she saw something else in her face: fear, palpable and strong, as plain as day. There is something inside Reign that Kara knows is dying, but if she can only reach it, and pull the humanity forward, she will have a chance at salvation.

    “Please, let me help--” Kara says through gasps of breath. She offers a hand, but Reign kicks it aside like a blade of grass. 

    “You can’t even help yourself,” Reign says from somewhere above Kara. A cold laugh sends an unpleasant jolt through Kara’s spine. “You’re a joke.”

    Kara feels the fire ignite in her chest, and she clenches her jaw as she focuses on standing up once more. When she picks up her head, she’s greeted by a powerful fist as Reign lands a punch that knocks her back on the ground. Kara stumbles, but she catches her balance quickly. She sits back on one knee, her shaky hands reaching for her nose as a hot liquid pours down her face. 

    Blood. 

    I’m bleeding , Kara realizes, startled. She has never seen her own blood before. Nothing on Earth, or in the Underworld, has ever been strong enough to hurt her like this. It makes her queasy, and she immediately turns away from her hand and tries to reset her doubling vision. As she does, she notices she’s positioned dangerously close to the edge of the roof. She chances a glance over the side, which does nothing to help her nausea, but it does distract her from the pain. She notices a figure exiting the palace and after a few seconds, she realizes who it is. Through blinking eyes, the two figures become one, and she watches as Lex slinks away quietly without so much as a whisper. He looks in both directions and snaps his fingers, before disappearing into nothing. 

    “No!” Kara calls out, reaching into the distance after a shadow, but it’s too late. Lex is gone, and Kara knows Lena is in more danger than before. Before she can properly react, she feels the steel grip close around her neck. 

    She places her hands over Reign’s, but they are immortally locked in a grip tighter than death. Kara strains against the pressure, choking as she gasps for air. She falls to her knees, clawing and scratching at Reign’s hands in a desperate attempt to free herself. Black spots begin to appear in front of her eyes, clouding her vision, and she realizes she’s being lifted off the ground completely by some otherworldly force.

    “You are no god, just as I am no devil,” Reign says, her voice thundering from somewhere Kara can’t make out. She feels the wind whipping around her as Reign holds her out over the ledge. She struggles to keep her eyes open, fighting with every last inch of strength to hold on. 

    “All I am is truth. And judgement. And death,” Reign snarls, looking at Kara once more with a threatening pause. Kara knows what comes next, knows the words, because she’s heard it over and over again in her visions. She struggles against Reign’s grip but the force only tightens the harder she fights. With a final pause, Reign smirks in her face before loosening her grip on Kara’s throat.

    “And I will Reign.”

    Before she can register what’s happening, Kara feels the wind whip around her, and then...nothing. 

    The next thing she knows she’s falling fast and heavy and far, and there’s nothing she can do to stop it. She tries to resist, but her body feels like lead, propelling down to the Earth faster than she can counteract. Flying seems impossible, and despite her best efforts, she can’t overcome her fatigue.

    The end is coming, and she wishes she could have done more, she wishes she could have fought harder. There are so many things she wishes she could do, but it all seems so empty now. She’ll never see her sister again, and the tears fall before she can stop them. A pair of emerald eyes flash before her, and she whimpers at the thought of being eternally separated from the goddess she fell in love with.

    Lena.

    Kara knows she failed, and because of that, her fate is worse than death. For if death is the only thing waiting for her now, it will be a cold and lonely existence. The Underworld has lost their queen, and Kara has lost Lena, and nothing will ever be the same again. 

    A scream echoes in the distance, and Kara feels it in her soul, but she can’t fight anymore. She doesn’t have the strength to reach out to the voice, so she lets the sound engulf her as her eyes finally close.

    “Kara stay with me!” A voice commands, and it’s so beautiful, Kara wants to wrap herself around it and stay with it forever. Through the darkness, she feels refreshingly cold hands on her face, and her neck, and her chest, and it reminds her of the flowing streams in the gardens on Krypton. She used to wade in the pools while her aunt told her fascinating stories about the old world order. Maybe when she wakes up, if she wakes up, she will be back on Krypton and this will all be a distant memory.

    “You’re going to heal,” the voice says gently, so gently, as soft flower petals caress her ears and cheeks. “I promise.”

    Through the balcony window, Lena watches in horror as Reign and Kara engage in battle. The golden chains around her wrists and ankles bind her strongly, too strongly, to her place, despite every attempt to break free. Lena mumbles every spell she knows, tries every bit of magic left in her arsenal, but everything fizzles and fades into nothing. Her powers are almost fully gone by now, so much so that Lex doesn’t find it necessary to keep her under guard. He knows she can’t escape, no matter what she tries to do. And, as a particularly nice gesture, she’s been given front row seats to Kara’s potential execution.

    “Come on, Kara,” Lena whispers, closing her eyes and picturing the golden face of the Titan she adores. “Please win.”

    Reign is deceptively fast, and stronger than she looks, and every punch lands heavy and hard against Kara’s body. She crumples against the strain of the fight, and Lena slams on the window pane in a futile attempt to feel anything. The chains rattle in warning.

    “Kara!” Lena cries out, but her words are vacuous, lost somewhere in space before they can ever reach Kara’s ears. It’s a special kind of torture to witness the battle and have no one hear her scream. She reminds herself to thank Lex especially hard for this particular gift he’s bestowed on her, if she should be so lucky to get a chance. 

    She waits with bated breath as Reign and Kara disappear from view and head to the roof. It feels like hours, though she’s sure it’s probably only minutes, before she finally sees Kara again. A flash of red and gold falls from the sky, faster and faster like an asteroid headed for Earth. Lena recognizes it at once. For a moment, she expects Kara to turn around and bolt back upright, but it never happens. Her descent is too fast, her limbs flailing like she’s lost control. Lena’s eyes fill with tears because she knows it’s Kara, her Kara, falling, falling, falling--

    “Fly, Kara!” Lena shouts, her chest bursting with terror. “Fly!”

    Everything in her body seems to explode as she watches Kara’s free-fall into chaos. She can feel a warmth spreading through her limbs, as the cracks of age along her skin get filled in with ancient power. She can feel her heart thumping wildly, strong and vital and permanent . She looks at her hands, trembling, as she recognizes the sparkling gold throughout her skin.

    Immortality. 

    The curse is broken, but Lena doesn’t wait to find out at what cost. 

    She lets out a piercing wail and the window shatters. Without wasting a second, she flies through the opening, unchained, her veins pulsing once again with the power of ancient gods. Her body feels charged and unbreakable, back to herself, which would be more of a relief if it wasn’t as a result of Kara’s peril. She reaches her hand toward Kara’s falling form and slows the trajectory enough to lower her to Earth on soft, tender wings. Lena glances at her fingertips, the way they sparkle in the sunlight and hum with magical power once more. She closes her hand into a fist and races forward.

    Kara’s body is laid gently on the ground and Lena appears at her side instantly. 

    “Kara, stay with me!” Lena cries, cradling her head in her hands. A splash of liquid falls on Kara’s forehead and cheeks, and the bruises and cuts instantly begin to heal. Lena’s tears fall on Kara’s chest and her hands, and the wounds continue to close. Her eyes remain shut, but Lena can feel a pulse, and she covers Kara in a shroud of protective darkness. 

    Reign lands with a strong thump behind her, and Lena turns to face her. She has every intention of ending the demon’s existence, and she’s confident with her powers restored she could do it swiftly. 

    “Ah, the mighty Queen of the Dead,” Reign scoffs, taking a step toward her. “You won’t be able to stop me.”

    “I’d avoid making idle threats,” Lena grins, holding up her hands as she begins to call on all the magic she possesses. The waves of magic churn in her hands as she swirls the power of the dead into a ball of chaotic fire. Before she can strike, she notices Reign’s face contort in horror as she stumbles backwards, away from where Lena is standing. Lena glances behind her slowly, and sees a horde of dead spirits coming to her defense, with a surprising figure leading them forward.

    “Mom?” Lena whispers, shaking her head. She forgets the incantations she’s been mumbling and drops her hands to her sides as she takes a tentative step toward them. “You came?”

    “I told you I would help you,” Lillian shrugs, as she signals for the crowd to stop. It’s a wild scene for Lena to comprehend: her mother at the helm of the Underworld, with the spirits following obediently behind, but it may just have saved them all.

    Lena catches Cat’s eye, and an indiscernible look passes between the two of them. There’s so much she wants to ask, so much she wants to say, but it will have to wait. There’s no time. Cat offers a small shrug and turns her attention back to the spirits to corral them back into groups.

    Behind her, a loud explosion goes off, like a jet taking off into the sky. She turns only to catch the last glimpse of Reign as she launches herself away, leaving a trail of smoke and ash behind.

    “Don’t worry about that, dear,” Lillian jeers, glancing up at the sky and then back at Lena with a glint in her eye. “We’ll handle that later.”

    “You’re going to heal,” Lena promises, kissing Kara’s forehead and placing a healing hand on her chest. “I promise.”

    Kara’s eyes remain closed, but Lena can feel the heavy beat of her heart, and it’s enough to keep her going. 

    “We’re going home now,” she whispers in Kara’s ear, kissing her gently. She waves her midnight cloak of starlight to cover them. A canopy of purple and white flames surround their bodies as Lena summons all the strength she has and pulls them back to the Underworld.

    As a result of the battle between Kara and Reign, the Earth falls into chaos. Everyone has turned further against Hades, the narrative skewed, unsurprisingly, out of her favor. The mortals are aware of the presence of gods, and they turn to Reign for their salvation. Her claims about Hades brings fear and resentment, as they’ve now borne witness to her atrocities and seen her pull the last known Titan back to the depths of the Underworld.

    There’s no mistaking the images: Hades, surrounded by a wall of fire, hovering over Kara’s lifeless form, dragging her greedily out of sight. 

    Deep in the Kingdom of the Underworld, away from the noise of Earth, the scene is a much quieter one: A heartbroken, lonely goddess holds vigil over the sick bed of her beloved.

    Kara stirs quietly, blinking her eyes awake after a long, tumultuous sleep. When her vision clears, she recognizes the warmth of her bed. She feels the fire from the hearth, and the soft, gentle fabric of the comforter she’s become familiar with. She sits up quickly, her body sore, but not broken. She sees a dark figure nestled towards the edge of the bed.

    “You’re back!” Kara exclaims, frantically throwing off the cover. She reaches her arms forward and Lena turns to accept her. “You’re you…”

    Kara runs her fingers over Lena’s perfect face, she feels the cold, strong marble of her jaw and the soft petals of her lips. Her eyes swirl with gold once more, her cheeks vibrant as she blushes. 

    “Oh, Kara, I’m so sorry--,” Lena says, her eyes fluttering in relief. “I never meant to gamble with your life, that wasn’t what it was. I don’t know how I can explain--”

    “You didn’t,” Kara assures her, cradling her face gently in her hands, as if holding a sacred offering. “You gambled with yours. Don’t you--” Kara pauses, turning her head away from Lena’s face and coughing, her lungs burning with exertion. She feels the ache in her ribs and she grimaces. “-- ever do that again,” she finishes. “I can’t lose you.”

    “Lie back down,” Lena coaxes, smoothing the rumpled creases Kara’s body left behind on the bed sheet. Kara obliges, but Lena remains close. She holds her hand firmly. “You won’t lose me, not ever, I promise.”

    “I almost did,” Kara whispers. She feels the sting of tears behind her eyes. “What did you think you were doing?”

    “I promised I would protect you,” Lena says, firm in her conviction. “I promised Astra, I promised myself. The world needs you, Kara Zor-El. But I failed. I didn’t think my brother would take the risk. And once he did, I thought for sure he wouldn’t be so foolish as to let Reign roam free. I should have known his arrogance would get in the way. He truly believed he could control her, despite knowing otherwise.”

    Kara coughs again, her breaths shallow and labored. She smiles apologetically at Lena. 

    “Enough about all that,” Lena says. “How are you feeling?”

    “Better,” Kara says, extending her limbs. Lena frowns, but Kara grins. “No, I am. Much better than before. I’ll be okay.” Kara pauses, rubbing her side where her ribs still feel tender. She felt them shatter against Reign’s fist, and it’s a miracle she can even lie still right now. She smiles gratefully at Lena. “Reign is strong. It felt like going up against myself. I don’t know what I would have done without the spirits. They held off Lex’s army so I could fight.”

    “I told you, you’re a marvel,” Lena hums, her fingers stroking over the lines of muscle in Kara’s arms. “You glow with strength. The dead flock to you, the power runs through your veins.”

    “Because of you--”

    “My power is only protection-- yours is something I have never seen before,” Lena says, shaking her head. 

    “Is it bad?” Kara frowns, but Lena clasps both her hands in her own. 

    “No darling, you could never be bad.”

    There’s a beat of silence as Kara stares into Lena’s eyes, lost in their magnificence. It feels like a lifetime since she’s seen her, and a slow, warm feeling of peace falls over them. 

    “What did it feel like?” Kara asks quietly, as she cards her fingers through Lena’s hair. The gray streaks are gone, replaced by a flowing mane of endless night. “To be mortal?”

    “Awful,” Lena chuckles, and Kara’s heart breaks. “It felt like I was just...fading. I always said I’m on borrowed time, but it’s a scary thing, to actually feel it. I didn’t know when the end was coming, but I knew it wasn’t far.”

    Kara looks at the ground, nodding thoughtfully. She doesn’t know what to say to that, only that she hates how close Lena came to true, real death. 

    “I think we both know the feeling a little too much,” Lena says, and Kara meets her eyes again. There’s a beat of silence before Kara replies.

    “We have to help her.” 

    That’s all she says, that’s all she has to say, because she knows Lena understands.

    “It won’t be easy.”

    “That doesn’t matter!”

    “I know darling,” Lena assures her. “I know.”

    “I can do it,” Kara says, confidently. “I can fix this. She isn’t evil. There’s something inside of Reign that still exists. I can save her.”

    “I think we both know what that something is, Kara,” Lena replies seriously, her eyes swirling in the darkness. She sighs, looking at Kara like she doesn’t want to say it first.

    Kara’s heart thumps against her chest, before sinking deep into her stomach. She knows what Lena is implying, but saying it out loud makes it all the more real. She recognized her when she saw her in person, but there was too much chaos surrounding them, too much tension, and before she could act, they were engaged in an all out brawl. But there was something in those eyes that Kara recognized, and she hates what it means. 

    “I know,” Kara says after a while. “I know it’s Sam. I recognized her despite the mask. But it’s all the more reason for us to try to help her. For Alex--” Kara chokes on the words, thinking of Alex and everything she must be going through. She wonders if Alex knows. She wonders still if she’s going to have to be the one to tell her. 

    “We’ll help Alex, and we’ll help Sam,” Lena promises. “I believe in you, but you have to understand: there are fates worse than death. I can’t send you in without understanding the potential consequences of this. If an immortal kills another, they send them into nothing. They cease to exist. I cannot bring you back. This time, we got lucky. I got to you before any real damage could occur.”

    Lena’s warning hangs heavily as Kara contemplates the risk. She knows Lena is reminding her of her own family, without saying so. There’s a reason they are no longer here, and Kara’s fate could be the same if she isn’t right about Reign. There’s a strong current of hope that burns in her chest and she knows she can’t ignore it, even if it means certain destruction.

    “I understand,” Kara sighs, she looks regretfully back at Lena.“It doesn’t change my answer.”

    “Then we’ll save Sam,” Lena nods. “But please, for now, let me have this.”

    Lena slides the covers back and angles herself gently in the space next to Kara, her body filling in the cracks like the perfect missing piece. Kara wraps herself around her, pulling her as close as possible and feeling the rhythm of her heartbeat as it pulses against her own. Their faces are inches apart, but neither of them speak. Kara allows herself to get pulled into Lena’s impossible force as she studies her perfect face, the face that no longer bears evidence of the scars of mortality. Kara buries her face in Lena’s neck so she won’t see the tears of relief as they stream down her cheeks. Lena holds her tight, and Kara’s senses overflow with the scents of sea salt and cedarwood and all things Lena. She closes her eyes and sighs with content.

    They still have a lot of work to do, but for now, they have this, and it’s enough. 

    Chapter 12

    Chapter Summary

    The finale: Lena and Kara vs Reign and Lex. With Lillian Luthor involved, can they finally settle this once and for all?

    Chapter Notes

    i can't believe we've come to the end of this journey - what a ride. i started this in 2017 or 2018(!?) really wanting to work on descriptive writing and world building more than anything else. i wish i could have written this faster, but i'm just proud to have come this far and now to finally have it complete. this universe has expanded beyond what i originally intended, but i think that's all part of the fun. of course, now with all the new characters that have been introduced in canon since i started this, i'd probably change a lot of things (and include andrea....naturally) but i'm still really happy that this version of kara and lena exist. who knows, maybe that leaves room for epilogues and one shots, new versions of the story etc. something is always cooking!

    i hope you guys find it satisfying and thanks for sticking with it (and, if you waited for it to be complete, sorry for making you wait for literal years - hope you enjoy this as much as i enjoyed working on it!)
