    When Kara wakes up the following morning, the bed is empty. She pauses, taking stock of every part of her body: her shoulders, her ribs, her hips and legs. Everywhere formerly battered and bruised is healed, the bones no longer broken. Hades’ tears have cleansed her. She runs her hands over the slight dip in the bed where the sheets still preserve the ghost of Lena’s elegant form. Kara’s mind is clear, her body strong. She feels a peaceful, complete calm, unlike any other she’s ever experienced. She flexes her fingers and smiles to herself, the power practically vibrating through her veins. It feels incredible to be whole.

    She takes a look around the room, noticing it for the first time since her return. It takes a moment before everything begins to register. The bedchamber is a disaster area: Everything is torn to pieces and Lena’s boudoir is destroyed. The mirror is shattered on the floor, the stool overturned with two broken legs sticking out at sharp angles. The wallpaper is ripped in various spaces, like a demon had burst through the doors and thrown a tantrum, clawing it beyond recognition. Kara frowns as she leaves her bed, gingerly walking around the ruins. She ducks under torn tapestry and steps over a long, jagged crack in the floor. She pauses at the door to her library. It hangs awkwardly, barely connected to the hinges. She doesn’t know if she wants to face what lies beyond it. There’s a very high chance everything she cherishes -- her only real possessions -- are destroyed beyond recognition. Kara swallows heavily and wills herself forward.

    The room is unrecognizable. The bookshelves, formerly crafted by Lena’s own expert hand, lie splintered in various layers along the walls. The books are scattered and torn. Bindings are ripped on the floor, pages turned to dust. The breath leaves her lungs as she gasps, falling involuntarily to her knees. 

    A large drop of water falls on the charred remains of a page as Kara stares, disbelieving, down at the wreckage. She sniffles, wiping at her eyes.

    It’s like losing her entire world all over again, and it aches .

    “Darling.” The velvety voice wraps itself around her, holding her close. Lena’s cool, gentle hand cups her shoulder. Kara sighs into it. “I’m so sorry.”

    “How?” Kara mumbles, blinking back another burst of emotion. She glances up at Lena. “How did this happen?”

    Lena’s eyes are dark, swirling with endless sadness. She frowns, her face breaking like all the pieces around them. “There was no one here to protect it,” Lena whispers. “We went to Earth and things fell out of balance. I failed.”

    Kara contemplates the destruction, picking up the sacred pieces of a destroyed Kryptonian text. The villagers had stormed to Earth at her call, a militia of dead souls willing to fight at her command. But it came at a price.

    “And it was like this when we got back? How did I not see--”

    Lena bites her lip and quietly affirms. “When we returned, the entire Kingdom had been upended,” Lena says. “My mother--” Lena pauses, her eyes swirling dangerously with sizzling heat. “Well, she isn’t one to do anything quietly, and certainly not one to accept small favors. I suppose I asked for this.” Lena sighs, her shoulders drooping slightly under the weight of her decisions. “I didn’t want you to have to face it right away. While you slept, I hid it so you could heal.”

    Kara lets out a mournful sigh. She appreciates being spared, if only temporarily, from the destruction. She knows it would be in her character to want to fix everything, even if her immortal body couldn’t take the stress. But now, she’s stronger. Now, she’s ready. 

    “You didn’t fail,” Kara eventually whispers, her fingers tracing over the partially disintegrated symbols. “You saved me.”

    Lena purses her lips together, a small smile appearing in the corner of her mouth. “We’ll fix this,” Lena assures her. “I’ll find a way to restore it. I promise.”

    “We have to fix everything,” Kara says, her mind made up. It isn’t about her own loss. She can move on from that. She’s done it before. But this is different. The fate of the cosmos rests on their shoulders. She pulls herself up and clenches her jaw, trying to make herself as big as possible. “I’m ready.”

    Lena studies her and the transformation is incredible. In an instant, Kara erupts into an indestructible force -- an unbreakable goddess, her formidable hero. Kara’s chest is proud, her immortal body the sturdiest structure in all the Underworld. She practically glows as she stares at Lena with determination and more love than is even comprehensible. 

    Lena’s heart beats strongly in her chest. She wants to remember her like this for the rest of time: infinite, unyielding. The last Titan.

    Kara nods at her firmly, imploring that they get to work.

    “I know how to save Sam,” Lena says after a pause. Her voice is whispery, echoing with the sounds of all the ghosts in the village.

    Kara’s eyes widen. The words take a moment to process. Kara watches the way Lena’s hands glide smoothly as she waves them over space, whispering incantations. In an instant, she produces a vial between her fingers. The contents swirl ominously, a charcoal black that is darker than death. Kara recognizes it immediately. 

    “What is that?” she asks accusingly, the bile burning at the back of her throat. Her guts twist, and her heart sinks. She knows exactly what it is, yet she wants so desperately to be wrong.

    “Black Kryptonite,” Lena says. Her voice doesn’t waver. She looks Kara in the eye, keeping her gaze strong.

    “Lena--” Kara takes a step backward, trying to create as much distance as possible from the poison in Lena’s hands. She feels her chest deflate slightly, her pride and strength punctured by the mere suggestion of using Kryptonite. Somehow, pushing aside her own losses seem comically easy, but facing her most feared weapon is a true test of her will. Her skin begins to crawl at the reminder of how deadly it is: draining her body of light, and sculpting her thoughts into clever ornaments of anguish and fear. Just having the substance in the same room sends her on a spiral. She feels the sticky, murky darkness begin to claw at her from the inside, like nails scraping along her veins. “No.”

    “Let me explain--” Lena says calmly. 

    “How do you even have that?!” Kara erupts, taking another giant step backwards. She points at it in disgust, her hand shaking.

    “I learned how to make it,” Lena shrugs, turning the vial over with grace. Kara flinches. “Or a version of it, at least. It has the same properties. A combination of the waters from the Styx and the Lethe, with the brimstone of Tartarus. The soil of Earth and a wisp of the clouds from Olympus. Only those that have ventured to all, may wield it.”

    “You’ve known this the whole time?”

    “Of course not,” Lena sighs, shaking her head. She seems disappointed, though Kara can’t be sure why. “I wouldn’t have kept it from you. I’ve been studying it for ages, trying to dissect it piece by piece. I never encountered this before you. I wanted to solve it, to make sure I understood everything about it in case it was ever used on you again. It has been my mission-- to protect you.” Kara swallows heavily at that. Her heart thumps painfully in her chest. “It wasn’t until I made my way to the depths of Tartarus that I learned the final piece. I’m only sorry it took me so long.” Lena turns it over once more, staring at it while in deep thought. “Why do you think I went so willingly with him?”

    Kara ponders. Olympus. She needed something from Lex’s kingdom. 

    “Ironically, the only thing missing was within my grasp the entire time.” Lena offers a sad smile. 

    Kara’s heart pounds in her ears. Lena swallows, and Kara studies the bob of her throat, the rhythmic pulsing in her neck. She doesn’t flinch or shy away from the solution. Instead, she simply waits. Kara loves her for her patience, her strength. But she hates that this is what she’s come up with.

    “Why this?” Kara asks, searching. There has to be another way , she wants to cry out. 

    “You only wore it on your skin, and you felt how powerful it is,” Lena explains. “If this is injected into Reign, it will force her out of Sam’s body. It will permanently separate them. Black Kryptonite is the only thing that can split apart their fusion.”

    “But there are risks ,” Kara protests, crossing her arms across her chest, like it will protect her from the grotesque substance in Lena’s hands. “We can’t just use this. It’s awful, Lena. Truly. And if Reign is really using Sam’s body as a vessel, there’s no way a mortal can stand it. No-- I can’t do it.”

    “I am not asking you to do it.”

    “You know what I mean,” Kara argues, gesturing toward Lena. “ We shouldn’t have to. This substance is destructive . I wouldn’t want to use this on anyone-- not even on Lex.”

    “I understand,” Lena replies gently. “And while I might not share that particular sentiment--” her eyes sparkle, and Kara can’t help a sad grin-- “If we use it properly, it can pull Reign and Sam apart. We can cure her. We can win.”

    “But how can we be sure? How can a mortal possibly withstand this?” Kara twists her lips, staring at the vial and back at Lena, pleading silently for an alternative. Lena’s face softens, as she subtly shakes her head. There is no other way to do this, and they’re running out of time.  

    Kara wants to believe her. And she almost does. She trusts Lena implicitly. But Black Kryptonite? She feels dejected as she stares at the ground. It’s hard to wrap her mind around the fact that the one substance in all the realms that can completely destroy her is being spun by the goddess who keeps her heart. She knows Lena won’t ever hurt her -- that’s not why she’s so torn. But just the idea of this poison falling into the wrong hands sends her into a frenzy. She can’t suffer under the influence of it again. If she does, there’s no telling what colossal damage she might inflict. The first time was a fluke, and it was a miracle that things didn’t end in tragedy. The second time, she might not be so lucky.

    “Nothing is ever certain, not even among the gods,” Lena tries to encourage. “But we have to try. What if Reign isn’t destroyed? Can we really risk that?” Kara is silent. Lena looks at the vial, her eyes swirling with intensity. She looks back at Kara with warmth. She reaches her hand out. “I wouldn’t propose it if I wasn’t absolutely certain it’s our only chance.”

    “I know.”

    “So…” Lena hesitates, blinking once. “Are you with me?”

    Kara inhales a deep breath. She glances at the liquid again, oozing and threatening despite its container. Her eyes trail up to meet Lena’s. They aren’t swirling pools of infinite magic anymore. They’re steady, and calm, with only the faintest trace of gold highlighting deep, emerald green. Kara’s hand touches Lena’s, and their fingers clasp together.

    She’ll follow Lena where no others could ever dare to venture.  

    “Always,” she says, and she means it more than ever.

     

    Xxx

     

    “Alex!” Kara calls as she knocks on her sister’s door. “Alex! Open up!”

    The trip to Earth was swift, faster than Kara can ever recall making it. The worlds seemed to blend together -- the living and the dead-- where time and space cease to exist. She simply blinked and found herself transported, standing on Alex’s doorstep, her face windblown and her lips still tingling from whispering Lena’s name. She glances briefly at the goddess to her right, catching a glimpse of those endless sparkling eyes with their infinite magic. They make her wonder if there will ever be a day that she knows all of Lena’s secrets. Kara’s chest warms at the idea of spending eternity trying to unlock them.

    She focuses again on her sister’s door, banging on it with little regard to her superior strength. The wood starts to crack under her power. Lena’s fingers tap her forearm with a gentle reminder: you’re on Earth now, love. Easy .

    Kara breathes a sheepish smile. There’s a faint shuffling sound behind the door. All at once, it bursts open with a loud ‘thud’. A frazzled looking Alex points a gun straight at the pair of them. 

    “Hands up!”

    “Alex!” Kara yelps, holding her hands up. “It’s just me!”

    “Kara--” Alex breathes, her shoulders drooping slightly. Then she pauses. Her eyes widen in disbelief as she notices the other figure in front of her. Her hands tremble as she points the gun in Lena’s direction. “What is she doing here?!”

    Kara immediately pulls Lena behind her, shielding her unnecessarily. It comes by instinct, before she even has a chance to think. She puts herself in front of the gun while staring hard at her sister. “Are you crazy? Put that away! She isn’t going to hurt you!”

    Alex hesitates. She doesn’t lower her weapon right away, even though they both know it won’t do any real damage. Kara narrows her eyes, silently forcing her sister to listen . Eventually, Alex concedes. She places the useless weapon back in the holster at her hip. She crosses her arms, her eyebrows still furrowed with distrust. 

    “Hello Alex,” Lena says warmly, stepping out from behind Kara. She offers her hand. “I’ve heard so much about you.”

    Kara is grateful for Lena’s last minute suggestion that they come dressed in their Earthly disguises. She can only imagine how Alex would react to seeing Hades in all her awesome power -- her sparkling robes and wild, flowing mane, combined with her swirling golden eyes. She almost laughs at the thought. She remembers her own reaction when coming face to face with the tremendous goddess. She recalls the way her immortal knees trembled, how her mouth ran dry. It was so transcendent, even for her, that she can’t imagine the effect on a mortal. 

    Even if that mortal is her big sister.

    Despite their efforts to remain conspicuous, Lena’s not meant to blend in. She’s dressed sharply and expensive, her porcelain skin in direct contrast with the midnight black of her tailored suit. Her lips are the deep dark shade of a pomegranate, her eyes sharp and calculating. Kara’s heart skips a beat. 

    “Mm--” Alex stumbles, her eyes fluttering and blinking rapidly. She doesn’t return Lena’s sentiments. “Am I--” she grimaces. “Dying?”

    Lena chuckles. “No, nothing like that,” she replies with a smile and Alex seems to relax slightly. 

    “It’s okay,” Kara encourages, reaching out and placing a gentle hand on Alex’s shoulder. “We’re here to help.”

    Alex nods and opens the door, allowing them inside with only the slightest hesitation. Kara and Lena follow her down the hallway. 

    Immediately, Kara is struck by how different everything feels. She knows her sister has been spending a lot of time at Sam’s house, but she is taken aback by how different Alex’s own space looks. There are pictures hung up by the entrance -- family photos, and one of Alex and Sam, heads leaned in together, smiling back out at the room like they haven’t a care in the world. There’s a welcome mat, and a coat rack with several garments on it. There’s a painting with explosive color that Kara doesn’t recognize, but finds bright and cheerful. She could never get Alex to take the time to decorate before, but apparently Sam’s more persuasive in that department. 

    There are long flowing curtains in the family room, and decorative pillows on the couch. There are trinkets and coasters, all falling within a navy and cream color motif that Kara knows her sister had nothing to do with. The place feels brighter. Cozier. Home.

    Sam Arias is all around them, and Kara’s chest aches. Lena must notice it, too, because she reaches for Kara’s hand and squeezes gently. 

    “You’re bold to come back here.” Alex takes a seat on her couch and gestures toward the TV. The news cast is blaring, playing the same images over and over. Protestors rage, holding up signs with Reign’s symbol on them. Grainy footage shows Hades, wild and desperate, pulling the lifeless body of Supergirl into the shadows. The ticker underneath praises Lex Luthor as Earth’s savior. “It’s a witch hunt.”

    “She saved me,” Kara says emphatically, motioning at the TV with disgust. “Lex isn’t going to protect them! This is all for show. They’ve got it all wrong. They always have it wrong.”

    “I know,” Alex sighs in defeat. She turns the TV off and closes her eyes for a moment. She breathes deeply before opening them again. Kara notices how exhausted she seems. Her strong, competent sister, the bravest mortal she knows, reduced to almost nothing. Her eyes are red-rimmed and bruised looking, her forehead permanently furrowed with anxiety.

    “What am I going to do?” she whimpers, looking at Kara for something -- anything. Kara’s heart breaks as she takes a seat on the couch next to her, pulling Alex close. 

    “This is all my fault,” Kara says. “I never should have tried to run. Even with the best intentions, I’ve gotten everyone I love in trouble.”

    “It wouldn’t have made a difference,” Alex argues, swallowing heavily. She’s on the verge of tears, and Kara can feel it. “Sam was always going to be part of this.”

    “What do you--” Kara starts, fumbling her words. She looks to Lena for help. 

    “Sam is Reign.” Alex says it with conviction, and Kara feels her stomach drop. “I can’t believe I didn’t see it sooner. I should have known-- I should have--”

    Alex’s words are cut off by a sob, and she leans further into the space between Kara’s arm and neck. Kara wraps her arms around her and stares at Lena over Alex’s shoulder. Lena’s eyes brim with tears.

    “How did you find out?” Kara asks cautiously.

    “I think I always knew,” Alex shrugs into Kara. She doesn’t lift her head. “I just didn’t want to face it. But once I saw Reign on TV -- the way she stands, the way she moves--” Alex’s breath hitches. She grimaces and tries to swallow. “It couldn’t be anyone else.”

    “You saved her,” Kara assures her, confidently. “You protected Sam, and she knows. She knows that.”

    “She doesn’t know it.” Alex’s voice is muffled. She pulls herself back to sitting and wipes at her eyes. “She doesn’t even know who she is. When I last saw her, she was forgetting everything. Big chunks of time. She couldn’t account for any of it. The worst part is, she doesn’t know she’s Reign. Or maybe she does by now, I don’t know. All I know is I’m the reason she got thrown in prison, and she must have been terrified. I didn’t want to leave her there all alone, but I didn’t know what else to do! And now she’s out there somewhere -- I don’t even know if I’ll ever see her again!”

    “Alex,” Lena says gently, kneeling down in front of her. She places a hand tenderly on Alex’s knee and everything stops. Alex’s tears stop flowing and the tension seems to leave her body. “You did the right thing. We’re going to fix this. We’re going to save Sam.”

    Alex twists her lips and nods. She covers Lena’s hand with her own. 

    “H-how?” she asks, glancing between the pair of them.

    “You’re not going to like it,” Kara warns. 

    “Just tell me,” Alex insists. “It’s not like it can get any worse, right?”

    Kara and Lena exchange hesitant glances before Lena takes over. She reaches into the innermost pocket of her blazer and pulls out the vial. She holds it up for Alex to see.

    “This,” Lena explains carefully, “is Black Kryptonite. It’s the same poison that was in Kara’s necklace.” Alex’s eyes widen as she looks to Kara for confirmation. Kara nods once with a solemn expression. “We are going to need to summon Reign and get her close enough to inject this into her. It is the only thing powerful enough to split her from Sam.”

    “But she’s -- unbreakable--” Alex frowns. “How are you going to be able to do that?”

    “It’s the only element in the universe that can weaken her. And--” Lena explains, the smooth muscles of her jaw rippling with warning. “She hasn’t faced me yet. I have my power back and can weaken her enough to allow the Kryptonite to puncture her skin.” Kara lets out a long exhale, but Lena ignores it. “I’ll need you both to help me.”

    Alex nods slowly. “Whatever you need.” 

    The automatic response catches Kara off guard. She expected more push back, but it sinks in just how desperate Alex is since she doesn’t even fight them. 

    “Alex--” Kara warns, trying to emphasize the severity of their actions. “There’s a chance we could lose Sam forever.” Lena shoots her a glare, but Kara shrugs. “She has to know,” she explains, and Lena eventually turns back to Alex. 

    “It isn’t foolproof,” Lena agrees. “Nothing ever is, unfortunately.”

    “If it works, will there be side effects?” Alex asks. “Will she remember? Will she have powers? Does it all go back to normal?”

    “I don’t know,” Lena answers honestly.

    Lena raises her hand in a somber send off. She might visit her one day. But not until everything has settled.

The figure walks tentatively closer, glancing from side to side with wide-eyed fascination. Lena feels the powerful heartbeat of the shadow, and knows at once they’re similar to her. She blinks again and recognizes the long, lean limbs and hesitant smile.

The landscape is endless and intimidating. The darkness is everlasting. The spirits are vibrant, the Kingdom infinite and powerful. She wonders what Sam will make of it all.

    Lena shakes her head, not entirely following Sam’s logic.

    “I’m so grateful to you, honest, but I don’t want this. I don’t want to live forever if Alex is going to remain mortal. I’d rather just live the rest of my days with her, and when she dies, I’ll join her here. We’ll be with the people we love. It’s as immortal as I’ll ever be.”

    Once Sam leaves, it feels like the entire Underworld utters a collective breath, the shoulders shifting and releasing an invisible strain that has weighed upon the land for thousands of years. The villagers have dispersed, going back to their quarters  in order to spend time with their loved ones. The world is quiet and peaceful, humming with an aura of calm that Kara has never experienced. She closes her eyes, feeling exhausted and renewed all at once. Lex is gone, and Lillian will never bother them again. Her sister has Sam back, and the land of the dead is restored to something beyond her wildest imagination. Everything is exactly as it needs to be.

    Later that evening, Kara’s eyes droop lazily as she allows herself to hover somewhere between planes of consciousness, aware but infinite and relaxed. It’s where sweet dreams have a habit of forming before taking flight, the rest of her immortal life stretching before her in grand layers. She feels protective arms cloak around her shoulders and she sighs into their embrace, knowing without a doubt that they belong to the beautiful goddess of death who has loved her since the beginning of time. 

    “Tell me I’m not dreaming,” Kara mumbles into her pillow, smiling in spite of herself. It feels too surreal to accept just yet.
